Para 1 — Headline numbers: AMCO delivered FY25 revenue of £70.9m — exactly at the pre-RNS consensus of £70.9m and +22% YoY — with adjusted EBITDA of £9.2m (+19.3%) and PBT of £4.1m (+145%). The primary catalyst is H2 momentum: H2 FY25 revenue was £39.1m (+27.0% YoY) and H2 basic EPS was 1.8p (+28.6% YoY), both confirming the acquisitive momentum from EMC (March 2025) and Electronix (July 2025) is translating into delivered numbers, not just modelled uplift. The adjusted EPS of 5.42p is a marginal miss of 0.08p vs the 5.5p consensus — immaterial and not a broker concern.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Pre-FY mode means H1 tracking (Phase 3.2) is retrospective/confirmatory and not scored — the operative signal is the strong H2 classification (revenue +27%, EPS +29%), both RNS-derived and unambiguous. The FY26 upgrade case rests on three pillars: (1) EMC and Electronix annualisation to full-year contributions; (2) B2B gross margin recovery from 33.3% toward sector norms guided as "incremental" in FY26; (3) EE margin recovery from 39.5% back toward 43.6% as WJ Projects rail electrification normalises and EMC project mix improves. The leverage position (interest cover 3.3x FY26fc, ND/FCF 6.6x) is the principal downside guard — any revenue shortfall translates non-linearly to EPS at this cover ratio, and IFRS16 lease interest (~£0.4m) further consumes the buffer. GridCore (acquired for £1, expected completion May 2026) is an incremental positive but its earnings quantum is unconfirmed.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are expected to hold FY26e EPS at approximately 6.9p (adjusted basis) and FY26e revenue at ~£76.5m; the in-line FY25 delivery and margin improvement language should prompt modest confidence upgrades for FY27 once GridCore and full-year acquisitions are modelled (+2–5% FY27e EPS potential). Consensus TP of 143p is currently equal to the 750p wait — AMCO is trading at consensus TP of 143p (close price 143p), leaving zero priced-in upside. Brokers need to raise TPs to 150–165p to provide any pull; this is achievable but requires them to credit the FY26 step-up with confidence. The key watch point is the FY26 H1 trading update (likely around July–August 2026): EMC margin normalisation and WJ Projects rail recovery will be the definitive signals. 🏁 Modest upgrade bias for FY27e; FY26e stable; stock at TP requiring a re-rating narrative — the FY25 delivery is solid but the upgrade cycle must now be earned through FY26 execution rather than assumed from the acquisition pipeline.

FY26e EPS bridge (FY2 = FY27) (1) Base: FY26e adjusted EPS consensus 6.7p — reflects severe trough year given continued market weakness (2) FY27e 12.0p = +79.1% step-up from FY26e 6.7p — this is a cyclical recovery assumption; structural step-ups from normalization of markets in EMEA/UK as rates fall and confidence returns (3) No acquisitions. The key watch point is Q2 results on 13 July 2026: if EMEA decline rate stabilises or improves vs Q1's −9.2%, and if the Middle East escalation is contained, the recovery thesis accelerates; if EMEA deteriorates further or France falls >14%, a formal EPS downgrade cycle recommences. 🏁 Cautious: Q1 in-line but with worsening qualitative signals on Middle East and no FY guidance anchor — brokers will trim modestly; structural recovery narrative intact but deferred.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: PROC delivered FY26 revenue of £85.5m — beating company compiled consensus of £83.5m by +2.4% and Sharescope FY1 fc by +4.3%, marking the highest revenue in the company's history and +23.0% YoY growth (+11.8% LFL). The single definitive catalyst is the H2 FY26 revenue confirmation: H2 delivered £51.4m (+24.8% YoY vs FY25 H2 £41.2m) — a genuinely strong half-year driven by 13 new stores (net 12), ecommerce LFL +21.2%, and the acceleration of paid social/content strategy. The group also outperformed the UK kitchenware market by +20 percentage points across the full year — a market share gain of compelling magnitude. EBITDA is "slightly ahead" of the £11.7m consensus and OP/PBT are "in line", with FX absorbing the EBITDA upside at the PBT level.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the scored signal is H2 momentum: classified 🟢 Strong (RNS-derived for revenue). The upgrade case is resilient because: (1) the revenue beat is structural (LFL growth + new stores), not one-off; (2) net cash of £4.4m (ahead of expectations) confirms the store investment programme is self-funding without leverage deterioration; (3) the RCF extension to £15m through April 2029 at higher levels than previously ensures the 100-store programme has adequate liquidity. Downside risk is contained by the LFL momentum (+11.8% full year) and market share gains — in a soft UK macro, consistent outperformance by +20pp is a structural advantage, not cyclical luck. FX is the primary unresolved risk: "significant FX volatility" impacted FY26 PBT, and PROC's unhedged or partially-hedged USD sourcing exposure means any further USD strengthening directly suppresses FY27 PBT.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are expected to upgrade FY26e revenue to £85.5m (confirmed actual), maintain FY26e EPS at ~2.1p, and upgrade FY27e revenue by +3–5% (toward £94–96m) and FY27e EPS by +7–13% (3.0p → 3.2–3.4p) on the higher revenue base and maturing store economics. Target prices are expected to rise from the consensus 53p to the 55–65p range — the current 36.6p price represents 50–78% upside to revised TPs. The first dividend (FY27e 1.80p) will attract a new investor constituency. The key constraint on a higher score is the unquantified FX headwind at PBT level (which prevented the EBITDA beat from flowing to EPS) and the IFRS16-adjusted leverage profile (ND/FCF 12.6x FY26fc), which caps the valuation multiple brokers are willing to apply. 🏁 Strong upgrade bias for FY27e estimates and target prices; the combination of a confirmed revenue beat, record trading performance, and net cash surprise is the best possible pre-full-results signal PROC could have issued.

Note: the large swing from £25.5m net debt at H1 to forecast net cash at FY reflects the £9.7m equity raise in September 2025. ND/EBITDA: 21.2x current (pre-raise distortion) / −4.9x FY25fc / −3.3x FY26fc. Interest cover: n/a. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash (post-raise, year-end position).

Including leases, the balance sheet carries significant leverage. ND/FCF including leases would be materially elevated. Flag for context but BOW convention is to report ex-lease net cash.

BOW · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue FY25 revenue: £31.3m (FY24: £36.6m) = −14.5% YoY. vs FY25e consensus £31.5m = −0.6% miss (essentially in line). Driven by 4 fewer restaurants (32 vs 36 at year-end) and challenging trading environment.

"Revenue of £31.3m (2024: £36.6m), a decrease of 14.5% in line with management expectations."

2. EPS / Earnings Adjusted loss after tax: −£1.7m (FY24: −£0.9m). Adjusted basic EPS: −0.20p (FY24: −0.50p). Reported loss: −£9.3m (includes £7.3m impairment + £0.05m lease modification loss). Adjusted EPS of −0.20p = in line with FY25e consensus of −0.2p.

"Adjusted (Loss)/profit for the year... (£1.7m) (2024: (£0.9m))... Adjusted basic (loss)/earnings per share (0.20)p (2024: (0.50)p)."

EPS quality check: Reported EPS −1.11p vs Adjusted EPS −0.20p. The gap (£9.1m = 0.91p) is entirely impairment (£7.3m) and lease losses. Tax rate = 0% (deferred tax assets not recognised against losses). No normalisation required — adjusted EPS is the correct base.

FY26e EPS bridge: (1) New base: FY25 adjusted EPS −0.20p; (2) Inorganic delta: nil (no acquisitions); (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: management guiding "improving trading performance" with LFL +5% in Q1 2026, refurbished sites +18.3%. If group revenue grows ~5% to ~£32.9m on 29 restaurants, EBITDA at ~£2.3m consensus implies flat/minimal EPS improvement; (4) Interest step-up: nil (net cash). Implied FY26e EPS: ~−0.1p, consistent with FY26e consensus −0.1p. No material revision indicated.

3. Adjusted EBITDA FY25 Adjusted EBITDA: £2.1m (FY24: £3.6m) = −41.7%. EBITDA margin: 2.1/31.3 = 6.7% (FY24: 9.8%). Margin compression driven by revenue decline and NMW/NIC cost pressures from April 2025.

4. Current trading & outlook LFL revenue: +6.1% in March 2026 (five weeks ended 29 March 2026). Refurbished sites: +18.3% LFL in same period. Group LFL for full Q1 2026 (quarter ended 29 March 2026): +5% YoY. Net cash at 13 April 2026: £9.0m (from £11.1m at year-end, reflecting ongoing investment).

"Trading has continued to improve since the start of the financial year, with like-for-like sales increasing by 6.1% in March 2026."

5. Capital structure & estate Net cash at year-end: £11.1m (FY24: £3.3m) — post £9.7m net placing proceeds. Current estate: 29 restaurants (reduced from 32 by three post-year-end closures of loss-making sites). No bank debt.

6. Acquisition pipeline "Active discussions with several potential exciting and scalable restaurant brand acquisition targets" — no financial quantum, no timeline, no terms disclosed.

"The Group remains in active discussions with several potential exciting and scalable restaurant brand acquisition targets."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification: Forward-looking language: "confident that 2026 will be an exciting year of rebuilding, refreshment and transformation." LFL growth data (+6.1% March, +5% Q1) is qualitative-directional without full-year guidance. No EPS guidance. "Macroeconomic pressures remain" is a caveat. NLW/Employment Rights Act from April 2026 are flagged as headwinds not fully absorbable.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — positive LFL trends disclosed but no numeric guidance upgrade, material cost headwinds acknowledged, estate still contracting. Provisional points: +1 to +3. No divergence — FY25 in-line, FY26 outlook similarly cautious-but-improving.

#1 and #2 Drivers: #1 — Current trading LFL: +6.1% in March 2026 and +18.3% at refurbished sites is the most forward-looking signal. Net cash £11.1m (now £9.0m) removes balance sheet risk narrative.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e Revenue: hold at £31.6m — LFL growth positive but estate is smaller (29 vs 32 sites). 5% LFL on 29 sites ≈ £31.9m; within rounding of consensus.
  • FY26e EPS: hold at −0.1p — NLW/NIC April 2026 headwinds partially offset by LFL growth. No material change.
  • FY27e: no consensus shown; unlikely to initiate upgrades at this stage.
  • TP: Cavendish covers (nominated adviser). TP 1.1p likely maintained — very limited upside case without demonstrated acquisition.

Conservative guidance read-through: No "not less than" language. The LFL data is directionally positive but management couches it with "whilst macroeconomic pressures remain." Brokers will treat this as confirming trajectory, not triggering upgrades.

Key risk: April 2026 NLW (+6.7%) and Employment Rights Act implementation will materially increase labour costs. Management acknowledges "cannot be fully absorbed." On a business with FY25 adj EBITDA of only £2.1m and thin margins, even modest cost step-ups could push EBITDA negative.

"The increases in the National Minimum Wage and implementation of the Employment Rights Act in April 2026 will again lead to higher labour costs that cannot be fully absorbed."

Para 1 — Headline numbers: BOW delivered FY25 adjusted EPS of −0.20p against consensus −0.20p — an exact in-line outcome. Revenue of £31.3m missed the £31.5m consensus by a trivial 0.6%, entirely consistent with the managed estate reduction from 36 to 32 restaurants. The real headline is the £11.1m net cash position post September 2025 placing, providing the firepower for the stated acquisition strategy. The H1 result (£15.1m revenue) was the weakest half since pre-Covid, with EBITDA H1 deeply negative at −£5.4m, but the H2 recovery to adjusted EBITDA of ~£7.5m confirms seasonality and operational gearing.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY25 revenue of £16.2m fell −7.4% vs FY24 H2 but the trajectory is improving — March 2026 LFL was +6.1% and the four refurbished Billericay/Ely/Epping/Lincoln sites recorded +18.3% LFL. This is the most important forward-looking data. However, April 2026 brings the NLW increase (+6.7%) and Employment Rights Act implementation — the company explicitly states costs "cannot be fully absorbed," creating a near-term EBITDA headwind against a business with only £2.1m of cushion. The acquisition pipeline is active but unquantified; any deal would consume a material portion of the £9.0m current net cash.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Cavendish (NomAd) will almost certainly hold FY26e estimates at −0.1p EPS / £31.6m revenue. The LFL trend is encouraging but insufficient to overcome April cost headwinds without quantification. TP of 1.1p will likely be maintained — implying 300% upside at current 0.275p, which itself reflects the speculative optionality value of the acquisition strategy rather than current earnings power. The score is capped at 38 by the combination of no upgrade momentum, structural lease leverage, NLW headwinds, and the fact that this is essentially a turnaround story in early innings. 🏁 Neutral — in-line delivery confirmed, LFL improving, but cost headwinds and thin margins prevent upgrade catalyst.

This is a gap of €6.1m — 44% below consensus on revenue, and an EBITDA guidance of ≥€0.5m vs consensus €4.3m. Brokers will be forced to reset FY26 models substantially.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: FY25 H2 of €3.7m grew +61% vs FY24 H2 — the strongest half in company history and consistent with the H2-heavy order execution pattern. The 10 simultaneous test orders with IPPs operating 10,000+ turbines is genuinely impressive and unprecedented. But tests are not orders — the company is explicitly building guidance on 50% conversion of these tests. The "at least" language provides a floor; if conversion exceeds 50%, revenue could approach €10m+. However, the consensus €13.9m would have required near-100% conversion plus additional sales, which management is not guiding to.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Zeus will cut FY26e Revenue from €13.9m to approximately €8–9m and FY26e EPS from 3.8p to approximately −0.1 to +0.2p (near break-even range). FY25e EPS will be trimmed slightly to −1.1 to −1.2p. No consensus TP exists, but fair value models will reset materially. The positive read: the pipeline is real, the test programme is at record scale, and the €7.8m "floor" represents 22% growth from FY25. The score of 28 primarily reflects the massive FY26 consensus reset required. 🏁 Cautious — FY26 consensus must be cut by ~44%; record pipeline is the silver lining but test-to-sale conversion remains the key uncertainty.

TICKER 9: ALU

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

Per the RNS: "Q3 FY25/26" covers the period to end March 2026. Market expects full-year FY26 results (September 2026 per Cavendish note: "Next results FY Sept").

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Q3 FY25/26 trading update — this is effectively a profit warning combined with strategic commentary).

"I see significant scope to drive performance through self-help initiatives, especially in our Water Management division."

Classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning — quantified downside (−£3.4m PBT), explicit guidance cut. Cautious macro language. Water Management self-help unquantified. "Approximately £11m" = floor-type language. Provisional points: −13.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Approximately £11m" for PBT is management's best estimate given current visibility. The order book (+28% YoY) provides medium-term structural support — this is NOT a structural demand failure. However, macro timing uncertainty means "approximately" could slide further. The Middle East crisis impact on project decision-making is ongoing and not predictably resolvable.

Key risk: Further project delays in Water Management — the unquantified self-help is the key uncertainty. If Changi Airport (first phase deliveries now delayed beyond FY26) and Chek Lap Kok (£1.3m risk of slipping to FY27) both disappoint in Q4, the £11m PBT floor could be tested. Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline is a quantified profit warning: ALU now expects FY25/26 underlying PBT of approximately £11.0m — down from Cavendish's prior estimate of £14.4m (−23.6%). This translates to adj EPS of approximately 22–23p vs the pre-RNS consensus of 29.0p (−21–24%). The primary driver is the Water Management division, where revenues were below expectations due to continued project delays exacerbated by macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty stemming from the Middle East conflict. The timing-specific nature of the miss is confirmed by the order book, which grew 28% YoY and 8% HoH to end-March 2026 — structural demand is clearly intact. However, order book growth is irrelevant to current-year earnings if projects are not physically commencing. The Building Envelope and Housebuilding Products divisions both delivered growth in challenging markets, partially offsetting the Water Management shortfall.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the implied H2 signal is the operative metric. FY26 guidance of ~£109m − H1 actual £50.4m = implied H2 of £58.6m (+4.6% YoY vs FY25 H2 £56.0m) — 🟡 flat/moderate and a meaningful deceleration from the H2-driven growth of prior years. The H2 EPS implied is approximately 14.1p (vs FY25 H2 13.7p, +2.9%) — essentially flat. The upgrade resilience is limited: Changi Airport (first-phase deliveries not commencing this year) and Chek Lap Kok (£1.3m at risk of FY26/27 slippage) represent identified downside risks to even the revised £11m PBT guidance. The self-help programme in Water Management — under new CEO Pamela Bingham — is unquantified and described as delivering benefits "from FY26/27 onwards," providing no in-year earnings support. H1 EPS of 8.1p represented only 27.9% of FY1 consensus — a −22.4pp deviation below seasonal baseline, the most severe H1 underperformance in recent history.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Cavendish (nominated adviser and joint broker) has already cut: FY26E adj EPS from 29.1p → 22.2p (−23.8%) and FY27E from 32.8p → 26.2p (−20.1%), reducing TP from 442p → 363p. Other brokers (Peel Hunt — joint broker) will follow with comparable cuts, pushing the full consensus FY26 EPS to ~22–23p and FY27 to ~26–27p. The pre-RNS Sharescope FY2 consensus of 33.0p will need to be cut by approximately −18–21%. TP consensus will likely fall from 426p to the 350–375p range. Current price of 260p represents 35–44% upside to the revised TP range — this is structural discount rather than re-rating opportunity. The watch point is the Water Management self-help programme: Pamela Bingham's "significant opportunities" in efficiency and productivity need to be quantified at FY26 results (September 2026) to establish credibility for the FY27 recovery. Until then, ALU is a value trap risk at 260p — the structural thesis (housing shortage, infrastructure backlogs) remains intact but the near-term earnings delivery is impaired.

🏁 Profit warning confirmed — FY26 EPS heading to ~22p (−24% vs pre-RNS consensus); FY27 also needs a −20% reset; double downgrade cycle; structural order book growth (+28% YoY) prevents deeper cuts but recovery timeline pushed to FY27/FY28; cautious/downgrades verdict.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

The RNS does not contain a "Currency Movements" section with explicit FX rate disclosures. With the share price at 550p vs a TP likely heading to £7.50+, the risk/reward remains attractive despite strong YTD performance.

🏁 Upgrade cycle starting — nuclear order momentum validates the structural thesis; H2 delivery near-certain at 95%+ order coverage; EPS upgrades likely for both FY26 and FY27; share price has room to close the discount to TP.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

Infrastructure: large frameworks deployment. Average daily net cash FY26 YTD: £445m (vs £372m same period FY25 = +19.6%).

Post period, the Group secured a new US government R&D contract exceeding $2.5m, further strengthening FY27 visibility. The initial commercial UPxi contract — a low-six-figure, four-month Phase 1 with a major systems integrator partner — is modest in scale but represents the first concrete evidence of the platform-to-commercial transition the bull thesis requires.

However, this is a pre-commercial stage business: there are no broker consensus estimates, no profitability guidance, and the CEO loan of $2.96m is the effective lifeline. The upgrade resilience is inherently limited by the absence of any consensus to revise, and the commercial transition from government R&D to scalable platform revenue remains largely unproven.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Tennyson Securities (sole broker) will update to $4.2m FY26 revenue (confirmed) and model FY27 at $7–8m based on backlog. 🏁 Neutral — revenue recovery confirmed (+40% FY26) and FY27 backlog provides visibility; but loss-making, CEO-loan dependent, and commercially embryonic on UPxi; no consensus to upgrade; speculative territory.

TICKER 6: TBTG

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY25 Full Year Results. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

TBTG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS = FY25 Full Year Results (year ended 31 December 2025). First full-year results since October 2025 IPO.
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 15.9p · Revenue £136.1m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 22.2p · Revenue £160.0m
  • Forecast broker momentum: Only 2 data points available (20 March 2026 and 21 March 2026) — EPS 16.1p, Revenue £136m. Essentially no broker momentum data; stock has minimal coverage history being IPO'd only in October 2025. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat, minimal history).
  • H1 baselines (1yr avg): Revenue: 43.0% (1yr avg; FY24 H1/FY = 43.5/101.1 = 43.0%). EPS: H1 history too limited and distorted (pre-IPO structure). FY1 fc Revenue £136.1m → baseline H1 rev = 43.0% × £136.1m = £58.5m (note: FY24 H1 was on old structure with third-party revenue).
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24 H1): Revenue £43.5m · EPS negative (pre-IPO structure)

⚠️ Sharescope EPS data anomaly: FY25 H1 shows 640.2p and FY25 H2 shows 333.4p. These are clearly wrong — actual FY25 EPS should be ~15p range per consensus. The Sharescope EPS history (1y ago H1/H2 showing −35.3/333.4) appears garbled — likely pence vs dollars conversion error or data loading issue. Using FY25 actual EPS from the RNS: basic EPS = £0.11 (11p) reported; adjusted EPS = ~27p (adj PBT £29.5m / ~110.7m shares). Consensus FY1 EPS 15.9p is pre-RNS; will assess vs actual in Phase 2.

  • Implied H2 YoY: FY1 fc £136.1m − H1 actual £52.2m = implied H2 £83.9m vs FY24 H2 £57.6m → +45.7% YoY — 🟢 strong.
  • FX: USD and EUR exposure significant — US largest market (39.8% FY25 revenue). Non-GBP exposure clearly >30%. Phase 0B required.

Phase 0B — FX: US & Canada = 39.8% of FY25 revenue (GBP). No Currency Movements table in RNS. GBP/USD: current spot ~1.32 (approximate April 2026). Prior year avg rate from RNS: not disclosed. The RNS notes: "The Group does not expect its growth ambitions nor cost base to be notably impacted by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East" — no explicit FX commentary on tariffs or rates.

US revenues are priced in USD but costs are mixed (manufacturing in UK/India; some US warehousing). The business is not purely USD P&L — it's primarily a GBP cost base selling into USD markets. GBP strengthening vs USD would compress GBP-reported margins. However: the company guided FY26 revenue "in line with market expectations" of £160.0m — this guidance is stated in GBP, implying any FX impact is already embedded or hedged.

Given: no currency movements table, but ~40% USD exposure. GBP/USD April 2026 ~1.32; FY25 avg likely ~1.28–1.30. GBP slightly stronger vs prior avg = mild headwind. However, the guidance is in GBP and in-line with consensus → applying missing baseline fallback: neutral band (±2c from prior avg = neutral). Apply mid-point of 30–35% exposure band → −4 pts. However, given the company's guidance is explicitly in GBP at £160.0m consensus and no currency headwind is mentioned in the outlook, this is likely already reflected. Applying Phase 0B override: company's guidance stated in GBP at £160.0m matches consensus — no incremental FX adjustment. No FX badge displayed. ±5pp confidence widening applied.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

TBTG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results (year ended 31 December 2025).

  1. Revenue — FY25 actual: £141.0m vs FY1 consensus £136.1m → beat of +£4.9m / +3.6%. Own-brand revenue £140.9m (+60% YoY vs FY24 £88.1m). Third-party revenue discontinued by design (fell to £0.1m from £13.1m). All five geographic regions grew >25%.

"Total revenue increased by 39.4% to £141.0m (FY24: £101.1m)"

  1. EPS / earnings — FY25 actual: Reported basic EPS £0.11 (11p) vs FY1 fc 15.9p — reported miss. However: adjusted PBT £29.5m (+98% vs FY24 £14.9m). Adjusted PBT consensus was pre-IPO at £24.8m (Sharescope FY1 fc PBT). Adjusted PBT beats consensus by £4.7m / +18.9%.

The 11p reported EPS vs 15.9p consensus gap: reported PBT £15.2m, impacted by exceptional IPO costs (£8.0m) and pre-IPO finance costs (£6.3m) — both non-recurring and fully expected. Adjusted EPS equivalent: adj PBT £29.5m less tax ~£5.9m (34.9% reported; ~25% normalised = £7.4m) = adj PAT ~£22.1m / 110.7m shares = ~20p adj EPS. This significantly exceeds the 15.9p consensus.

Tax rate gate: Effective rate 34.9% vs normalised ~25% (UK statutory). Deviation = +9.9pp > 3pp threshold. Restated adj EPS at 25% normalised: adj PBT £29.5m × (1−0.25) / 110.7m shares = ~20.0p. Reported 11p is depressed by the 34.9% effective rate caused by non-deductible IPO costs. The 34.9% rate will normalise in FY26. 🚨 Tax-distorted year — FY25 reported EPS understates underlying. Use ~20p as the true underlying base for bridge.

  1. FY26e EPS bridge:
  • (1) New base EPS: ~20p (adj, normalised tax from FY25).
  • (2) Inorganic: nil.
  • (3) Revenue growth: FY26 guidance = £160.0m (consensus). Gross margin maintained at ~62.7% → gross profit ~£100.3m. EBITDA guided: company says "profit ahead of expectations" while revenue in line at £160.0m. Consensus EBITDA FY2 = £38.3m.
  • (4) Interest: pre-IPO finance costs (£6.3m) fall away entirely in FY26. Only lease/other interest (£0.5m ongoing). This is the key EPS driver — the removal of £6.3m interest charge + £8.0m exceptional IPO costs = £14.3m additional pre-tax flowing through FY26 vs FY25 reported.
  • (5) Tax normalisation: from 34.9% to ~25%.
  • Implied FY26 EPS (reported basis): Adj PBT ~£29–32m (revenue growth + margin) minus zero bank interest (post-IPO) → reported PBT ~£28–31m × (1−0.25) / 110.7m shares = ~19–21p reported EPS vs FY2 consensus 22.2p. The company says "profit ahead of expectations" for FY26 → implies above 22.2p, suggesting actual FY26 adj EPS heading to 23–26p (+3–17% above consensus).
  1. Order book / forward visibility: Q1 FY26 "very encouraging start... strong growth across the Group's core business and across all key markets." Tria Laser relaunched March 2026. ZIIP FY27 targeted as "breakthrough year." 40+ product pipeline.

"Very encouraging start to Q1 FY26, with strong growth across the Group's core business and across all key markets and channels"

  1. Margin / profitability: Gross margin 62.7% (+590bps vs FY24 56.8%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 26.6% (+400bps). FCF conversion 91.7% of adj EBITDA. Operating ROCE >50%. Balance sheet: net cash £40.8m, zero borrowings.
  2. Capital: No dividend (policy under review as business matures). Net cash £40.8m (vs net debt £27.1m FY24 = swing of ~£68m from IPO). £12.5m undrawn working capital facility (extended from £5.0m in March 2026).
  3. Qualitative tone — FY26 outlook: "Revenue in line with current market expectations [£160.0m]... due to stronger margins, it is anticipated that profit will be ahead of expectations." This is explicit upgrade-triggering language for FY26 profit.

"due to stronger margins, it is anticipated that profit will be ahead of expectations"

EPS quality check: See above. 34.9% effective rate for FY25 restated to ~25% normalised. Adj EPS ~20p is the correct base. FY26 removes all non-recurring costs (£14.3m combined IPO + pre-IPO interest). FY26 will show dramatically improved reported EPS even on identical underlying performance.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

FY26: Revenue "in line with market expectations" (£160.0m) + "profit ahead of expectations." This is the clearest possible split-guidance signal.

Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — explicit "profit ahead of expectations" for FY26. Revenue in-line but margin beat driving profit upgrade. Exceptional balance sheet (£40.8m net cash, zero debt). Q1 FY26 "very encouraging." Provisional points: +14.

Divergence check: FY25 revenue beat (+3.6%) but reported EPS missed (11p vs 15.9p). The miss is entirely IPO/pre-IPO non-recurring costs. Outlook is explicitly better than expectations. Divergence: reported EPS miss but adj EPS significantly ahead + profit ahead guidance for FY26. Flag: 🟡 Beat quality — reported EPS miss is structural (one-off costs), not operational. Adj EPS ahead. Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline is the combination of a +3.6% revenue beat (£141.0m vs £136.1m consensus) and the explicit FY26 guidance that "profit will be ahead of expectations" due to stronger margins. FY25 adjusted EBITDA reached £37.5m (+63.8% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 26.6% — 400bps above FY24's 22.6%. Reported basic EPS of 11p missed the 15.9p consensus, but this miss is 100% attributable to non-recurring IPO exceptional costs (£8.0m) and pre-IPO interest (£6.3m) that will not recur in FY26. On a normalised adjusted basis, TBTG delivered approximately 20p EPS — a material beat. The balance sheet transformation from net debt £27.1m (FY24) to net cash £40.8m (FY25) removes all financial risk and enables investment-led growth with zero reliance on external funding.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the H2 signal is striking: FY25 H2 delivered £88.8m revenue (derived: £141.0m − £52.2m H1), a +54.2% YoY improvement vs FY24 H2's £57.6m — well ahead of the seasonal pattern. For FY26, implied H2 of ~£101.5m (£160.0m FY2 guidance − ~£58.5m H1 baseline) represents +14.3% YoY — firmly in the 🟢 strong category. The upgrade resilience is structural: the removal of £14.3m of non-recurring costs (IPO exceptional + pre-IPO interest) from the FY26 P&L creates a permanent earnings uplift independent of topline growth. Even if FY26 revenue grows at only 10% (below the £160.0m guidance), the non-recurring removal alone drives reported EPS well above FY25's 11p. The margin thesis (62.7% gross margin, +590bps trend) and the 91.7% FCF conversion at operating ROCE >50% confirm this is not a revenue-dependent story — the quality is embedded.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will raise FY26 EPS from 22.2p → ~23–26p (+4–17%) as the non-recurring cost removal flows through and margins sustain above prior assumptions. Revenue held at £160.0m (company guidance). Target prices likely in the 450–550p range for initiating brokers — the 55% current discount to 470p consensus TP is primarily a coverage gap that today's full-year results presentation will begin to close. The key watch point is Tria Laser commercial traction following its March 2026 relaunch — the brand contributed only £2.0m in FY25 but is targeted as a "meaningful scaling opportunity" in FY26. If Tria gains early US distribution momentum, FY26 revenue could exceed £160.0m, driving a second upgrade cycle. The tariff risk on US revenues (39.8% of group) via potential USD import duties is the structural watch point for FY26/FY27, mitigated by the Indian manufacturing investment underway.

🏁 Strongly positive — FY25 adj EBITDA beat, explicit FY26 profit-ahead guidance, £14.3m non-recurring removal transforms reported EPS; price at 303p represents 55%+ discount to fair value; upgrade cycle starting as coverage builds post-IPO.

DSCV

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY update accordingly. Next year end = 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

DSCV · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Incoming RNS = pre-FY trading update. Market focused on FY26 full-year outturn and FY27 outlook.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 40.3p · Revenue £445.3m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 43.7p · Revenue £472.0m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change +6.9% over snapshot period (37.7p → 40.3p). Upgrades driven by June 2025 step-up (+2.5p). Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat since early February). Revenue broadly stable at ~£444–445m. No downgrade events visible.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.1% of FY = £223.0m · EPS 49.9% of FY = 20.1p (using 2yr avg per data)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £211.1m · EPS 18.4p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): Revenue: FY26e £445.3m − H1 actual £216.4m = implied H2 £228.9m vs FY25 H2 £211.8m → +8.1% YoY. EPS: FY26e 40.3p − H1 actual 19.5p = implied H2 20.8p vs FY25 H2 20.3p → +2.5% YoY
  • FX: Phase 0B check — DSCV is a multi-currency business (USD, EUR, Nordic currencies). RNS Note 1 discloses: GBP strengthened 5% vs USD, weakened 3% vs EUR, weakened 5% vs Nordic currencies for the full year. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues per disclosed divisional geography. Phase 0B FX Rule 1 (single currency >30%) does not fire. However, the mixed FX environment (USD headwind, EUR/Nordic tailwind) is approximately offsetting — reported growth = CER growth (both +5%), confirming nil net FX impact. Phase 0B constant currency override applies: reported +5% = CER +5%. No adjustment.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: FY23 £73.6m / FY24 £227.5m / FY25 £216.2m / Current H1 £121.4m → FY26fc £125.0m → FY27fc £109.4m · ND/EBITDA: FY25 1.7x / current 1.6x / FY26fc 1.6x / FY27fc 1.3x · Interest cover FY26fc: 6.6x · ND/FCF FY26fc: 3.9x · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — leverage manageable and declining; 6.6x interest cover; no revision risk from balance sheet.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

DSCV · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update

  1. Revenue — Full year: Full year Group sales increased by +5% (both reported and CER), with +2% organic growth and +3% from acquisitions. No explicit revenue figure stated. Implied FY26 revenue = £445.3m × 1.00 (consensus already at +5% YoY). Consensus of £445.3m appears consistent with the +5% guidance; no beat/miss calculable as no hard figure disclosed.

"Full year Group sales increased by 5% (both reported and CER) and by 2% organically, with a 3% contribution from acquisitions."

  1. Revenue — Q4 acceleration: Q4 sales +6% CER, +5% organically. Acquisitions contributed 1%. This represents an acceleration vs. the full-year average of +5% CER, confirming momentum building into year-end.

"Group sales in the fourth quarter increased by 6% CER and by 5% organically. Acquisitions contributed 1%."

  1. Orders — Strong leading indicator: Full year orders +9% CER, +5% organically. Order book grew +6% over the first half (i.e. from H1 to H2). Q4 orders +16% CER, +15% organically — "ahead of sales for the third consecutive quarter." Customers increasing short-term demand and extending order periods.

"Group orders in the fourth quarter increased by 16% CER and by 15% organically and were ahead of sales for the third consecutive quarter, with customers increasing both their short-term demand and extending order periods."

  1. EPS / earnings: EPS "in-line with consensus market expectations." Company-compiled consensus for adjusted EPS = 40.1p (per footnote 3 of RNS). Sharescope FY1 fc = 40.3p. The in-line confirmation is a 0.0–0.5% variance — no beat, no miss.

"The Group on-track to deliver another year of growth in adjusted earnings per share in-line with consensus market expectations. Company compiled consensus for adjusted earnings per share is 40.1p."

FY27e EPS bridge (construct here, reference in Phase 4 #2):

  • (1) New base EPS actual: 40.1p (company consensus; Sharescope FY1 fc 40.3p — use 40.1p as disclosed)
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: Trival Antene (acquired April 2026, just post year-end). Disclosed as "Slovenian-based designer and manufacturer of communication antennae and masts." No revenue/profit quantum disclosed in this RNS. Proforma gearing moves from 1.2x to 1.7x, implying Trival EBITDA contribution adds ~£8–10m EBITDA at current run-rate. Very small relative to Group EBITDA of ~£76m. Annualisation delta: modest positive, estimate +0.5 to +1.5p EPS in FY27. Flagged as unquantified — low confidence.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: Q4 orders +15% organically; FY orders +5% organically. Organic revenue growth guides to +2% FY26, but order book growth of +9% CER suggests FY27 organic revenue could accelerate toward +4–6%. Applying +4% organic revenue to FY26 EBITDA base of ~£76m with modest margin improvement → EBITDA uplift ~£3–4m → EPS delta ~+1.5 to +2.0p
  • (4) Interest step-up delta: Net debt declining (£216m FY25 → £125m FY26fc → £109m FY27fc). Finance costs reducing. RNS explicitly references "reducing interest costs." Positive delta: +0.3 to +0.5p
  • Implied FY27e EPS: 40.1p + ~0.5–1.5p (Trival) + ~1.5–2.0p (organic) + ~0.3–0.5p (interest) = ~42.4–44.1p. Current Sharescope FY2 fc = 43.7p — broadly consistent, no material revision indicated from this RNS alone. Trival upside is the swing factor.
  1. Gross margins: "Gross margins remain robust, reflecting the strength of our differentiated value proposition." Qualitative only — no margin figure disclosed for FY26.

"Gross margins remain robust, reflecting the strength of our differentiated value proposition."

  1. Gearing / balance sheet: Year-end gearing expected at c.1.2x (pre-Trival). Pro-forma including Trival: c.1.7x — "comfortably within our target range." Strong operating cash flow flagged.

"With continuing strong operating cash flow, year-end gearing is expected to have reduced to c.1.2x, with proforma gearing including Trival, expected to be c.1.7x, comfortably within our target range."

  1. Acquisition — Trival: Regulatory approval received; completion occurred "earlier this month" (April 2026). Slovenian manufacturer of communication antennae/masts for defence and industrial markets. Bolt-on; no financial quantum disclosed.

"Regulatory approval for the acquisition of Trival Antene d,o,o ('Trival'), announced on 4 December 2025, has been received and completion occurred earlier this month."

  1. Capacity investment: New production facility in Thailand (further investment), new enlarged facility in India (due to complete in H1 of new financial year — FY27 H1). Additional engineering and sales capacity in US and Europe. Implies capex slightly elevated in FY27 H1.

"We made additional investments this year in operating capacity, with further production in Thailand and a new enlarged facility in India, due to complete in the first half of the new financial year."

  1. Qualitative tone / outlook: "A number of acquisition opportunities in development." Order book grew +6% over H1. "Very well placed for further resilient growth."

"The Group has a number of acquisition opportunities in development and along with our pipeline of organic opportunities and design wins, it is very well placed for further resilient growth."

EPS quality check: No disclosed EPS figure (trading update only). Company-compiled consensus 40.1p confirmed "in-line." No tax rate distortion visible. No exceptional income. No quality flag required.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward-looking language covers FY27 (the next financial year). Key phrases: "very well placed for further resilient growth"; order book +9% CER; Q4 orders +16% CER (+15% organic); customers "extending order periods"; new Trival acquisition just completed; India facility completing H1 FY27 adding capacity; "reducing interest costs" supporting earnings.

The guidance is qualitative only — no numeric FY27 EPS or revenue target stated. However, the order book momentum (+15% organic Q4 orders) is strong forward signal. "Not less than" language absent. "In-line with consensus" is the explicit EPS anchor for FY26; FY27 language is bullish but qualitative.

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — confident qualitative language with visible earnings drivers. Points: +6 to +8. No numeric upgrade trigger. Order book acceleration supports upgrade cycle probability but requires confirmation at prelims (3 June 2026).

Exact guidance phrase: "very well placed for further resilient growth" · Qualitative only · Covers FY27 and medium-term · Classification: Constructive · Provisional: +7 pts

No divergence: FY26 in-line delivery with constructive FY27 outlook — consistent direction.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

3.3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — scored)

Revenue: RNS confirms +5% growth → implied FY £445m approx. H2 revenue = £445.3m − £216.4m = £228.9m. Using RNS-derived FY figure for EPS; consensus-derived for revenue — both flagged.

  • Implied H2 revenue: £228.9m vs FY25 H2 £211.8m → +8.1% YoY → 🟢 strong (>+10% threshold nearly met; above +5% moderate threshold). Classification: 🟢 strong (borderline; call it moderate-to-strong)
  • Implied H2 EPS: 20.6–20.8p vs FY25 H2 £20.3p → +1.5 to +2.5% YoY → 🟡 moderate (0–10%)

The H2 revenue recovery (+8.1%) is the stronger signal. EPS H2 YoY of +1.5–2.5% reflects the higher H2 comp from FY25 (H2 FY25 was a strong +15.3% EPS growth half). This is not a concern — the absolute H2 EPS delivery is in line.

Profit warning feasibility gate: not applicable (positive H1 tracking, no H1 miss).

3.4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: +6.9% net change over snapshot period (37.7p → 40.3p). Upgrades concentrated in June 2025 (preliminary results event), adding ~2.5p. No upgrades or downgrades since early June 2025. Stable for 10+ months.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STEADY (FLAT per Sharescope)
  • Revenue trend: Broadly stable; minor fluctuations around £444–446m over the period.
  • Divergence: None. Share price has drifted from ~884p to 873p (−1.2%) while consensus stable. Price softness vs. stable forecasts suggests mild re-rating rather than fundamental concern.

3.5. Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP.

  • Net debt (£m): FY23 £73.6m / FY24 £227.5m / FY25 £216.2m / H1 FY26 £121.4m / FY26fc £125.0m / FY27fc £109.4m

Note: Large net debt increase FY23→FY24 (£73m→£228m) reflects acquisition activity. Now deleveraging. Pro-forma Trival adds ~0.5x to FY26 gearing (1.2x → 1.7x) but remains within target range. Interest costs explicitly declining per RNS — a positive EPS driver.

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — not quite net cash but trajectory is clearly deleveraging; 6.6x interest cover; no revision risk from balance sheet.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26e vs FY25 actual:

  • FY26fc EPS 40.3p vs FY25 38.7p → ✅✅ FY26fc EPS growing +4.1% vs prior year actual
  • FY26fc Revenue £445.3m vs FY25 £422.9m → ✅✅ FY26fc Revenue growing +5.3% vs prior year actual

Step 2 — FY27e vs FY26 consensus:

  • FY27fc EPS 43.7p vs FY26fc 40.3p → ✅✅ FY27fc EPS growing +8.4% vs FY26fc
  • FY27fc Revenue £472.0m vs FY26fc £445.3m → ✅✅ FY27fc Revenue growing +6.0% vs FY26fc

3.6. Structural / One-off Flags

Order book acceleration: Q4 orders +15% organically is the strongest quarterly organic order growth signal in the disclosed series. Combined with "customers increasing both their short-term demand and extending order periods," this implies a structural demand recovery cycle entering FY27 — not a one-off.

"Group trading accelerated in the fourth quarter with all operating units experiencing a strong sequential increase in demand, reflected in both orders and sales."

Trival post-year end: Defence/industrial antenna acquisition adds a new end-market exposure. Small relative to Group but diversifies further into defence thematic.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

DSCV · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

#1 and #2 Drivers:

#1 — Order book / Q4 demand acceleration. Q4 organic orders +15%, full year orders +9% CER — this is the dominant broker note driver. Brokers covering DSCV focus intensely on orders vs. sales ratio as the leading revenue visibility signal. Orders ahead of sales for three consecutive quarters, with order book growing +6% through H2, strongly implies FY27 revenue upgrades. This is the single most influential metric in the RNS.

#2 — FY26 EPS in-line confirmation + gearing reduction. The confirmation of EPS in-line with 40.1p consensus removes downside risk and, combined with gearing falling to 1.2x (pre-Trival), signals financial capacity for further M&A. Brokers will note the improving balance sheet trajectory as an enabler of the upgrade story.

#2 Forecast revisions (FY26 and FY27):

FY26: Revenue — hold (consensus already at +5%, RNS confirms +5%). EPS — hold to marginal upgrade (+0–1%; company consensus 40.1p, Sharescope 40.3p — negligible variance). Brokers likely to mark FY26 as delivered in-line; minimal revision.

FY27: This is where broker action is most likely. The FY27e EPS bridge (constructed Phase 2) implies ~42.4–44.1p vs Sharescope consensus 43.7p — broadly in line, but with upside risk from Trival annualisation. Revenue: FY27e £472m could see modest upgrades (+1–3%) given Q4 order momentum. EPS: +0 to +3% upgrade range, with higher probability around +1–2%. Trival is the unquantified swing factor — once financials are disclosed at the 3 June prelims, FY27 estimates could move more meaningfully.

#3 Target price and recommendation: Brokers likely to hold or marginally raise TPs. Current consensus TP 873p = 51% premium to 578p close price. Gap remains very wide, suggesting the stock has already de-rated significantly. Expect TPs in range 860–920p to be maintained or gently upgraded on order book strength. No recommendation changes expected from a trading update that delivers in-line.

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: "In-line with consensus" is neutral guidance language. "Very well placed for further resilient growth" and the order book narrative are the bullish signals. Brokers will interpret the Q4 orders (+15% organic) as deliberately underplayed — the standard DSCV communications style is measured rather than promotional. This increases upgrade cycle probability for FY27, particularly post-prelims on 3 June.

#5 Key risk: The FX headwind on USD (GBP +5% stronger vs USD in FY26) resumes as a risk if GBP continues to strengthen. USD-denominated business from US engineering/sales investment could face a translation headwind. Separately, the India facility completing H1 FY27 adds capex/depreciation before fully contributing revenue.

"We made additional investments this year in operating capacity, with further production in Thailand and a new enlarged facility in India, due to complete in the first half of the new financial year, along with additional engineering and sales capacity in the US and Europe."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: hold (in-line). FY27 revision: modest upgrade bias. Tone label must be consistent: upgrade bias → Constructive. ✓

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely — primarily a FY27 story driven by order book momentum and Trival optionality; FY26 in-line delivery provides stable base.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

67/100 · Confidence: 62–72 · No FX adjustment · 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

ComponentPts
🟢 Q4 order acceleration: +15% organic, orders > sales 3rd consecutive quarter+14
🟢 FY26 EPS in-line confirmed (40.1p company consensus)+8
🟢 Gearing reduced to 1.2x; interest costs declining; supports EPS progression+7
🟢 Constructive FY27 outlook: "very well placed for further resilient growth"+7
🟢 Revenue trajectory reversal: +5.3% FY26e after two years of contraction+6
🟢 Trival acquisition complete: defence/industrial antennae adds FY27 annualisation delta+5
🟡 FY26 EPS in-line only (not a beat); no explicit beat language−3
🟡 Implied H2 EPS modest YoY (+1.5–2.5%); FY25 H2 was a strong comp−2
🔴 No FY27 numeric guidance; Trival quantum undisclosed; full upgrade requires 3 June prelims−5
🔴 Share price already at 34% discount to consensus TP — implies market has not yet re-rated−5
🔴 Capex elevated (India facility) in FY27 H1; USD headwind risk if GBP re-strengthens−3

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The definitive catalyst in this RNS is the Q4 order acceleration: organic orders +15% in Q4, full-year orders +9% CER. This represents a clear demand recovery cycle, with orders ahead of sales for three consecutive quarters and customers explicitly extending order periods — the most constructive demand signal DSCV has delivered in several years. FY26 full-year revenue growth confirmed at +5% (reported and CER), matching consensus of £445.3m exactly. FY26 adjusted EPS delivered in-line with the company's own compiled consensus of 40.1p. The revenue turnaround from two years of contraction (FY24 −2.7%, FY25 −3.2%) to +5.3% is structurally significant and now running ahead of the most recent consensus.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the key metric is implied H2 momentum. Implied H2 revenue of £228.9m represents +8.1% YoY versus FY25 H2 — confirming the recovery was not front-loaded. Implied H2 EPS of ~20.6–20.8p is +1.5–2.5% YoY against a strong FY25 H2 comp (+15.3%). The modest H2 EPS growth rate is not a concern — the base effect from FY25 H2 was unusually strong. The upgrade story into FY27 is structurally intact: the order book grew +6% through H2, the India capacity facility completes in H1 FY27, and the Trival acquisition (completed April 2026) adds incremental annualisation income. Balance sheet gearing at 1.2x pre-Trival provides room for further bolt-on M&A. Downside containment is strong — there is no guidance miss, no margin warning, and no EPS downgrade from the RNS.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are most likely to hold FY26 estimates (EPS 40.1–40.3p, revenue ~£445m) and make modest upgrades to FY27 in the range of +1–3% EPS (43.7p current → 44–45p plausible). The Trival acquisition quantum is unknown and will be the key swing factor at the 3 June prelims. Revenue FY27 could see +1–2% upgrades given Q4 order run-rate. TP maintained or gently raised from 873p consensus — range 875–925p expected. The main watch-point is the 3 June preliminary results, which will disclose Trival financials, gross margin for FY26, and will be the event that drives the more material upgrade cycle. The current discount (share price 578p vs TP 873p = 51% premium) implies substantial re-rating potential if the order momentum is confirmed.

🏁 Q4 organic orders +15%, order book +9% CER, three consecutive quarters of orders ahead of sales — a clear demand recovery in motion. FY26 delivered in-line; FY27 upgrade cycle probable at June prelims. Score 67/100.

ESYS

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results accordingly. Next year end = 31/7/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Note: ESYS is subject to a recommended cash takeover offer at 17p per share (unconditional deadline 8 May 2026). This fundamentally changes the analytical context — broker revision predictions are largely moot if the offer becomes unconditional. The scorecard is completed for completeness but the score should be interpreted in light of the takeout context.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The defining fact of this H1 FY26 report is not the financials but the context: a recommended cash offer at 17p per share from founder Mark Furness, with an unconditional deadline of 8 May 2026. The share price at 16.65p represents a 2% discount to the offer — the market is pricing a small probability of lapse. Against that backdrop, the H1 results show revenue declining −25% to £7.8m (−23% constant currency), with Run Rate ARR falling −24% to £12.7m. The primary driver is the continued downsizing of a single large North American strategic customer plus the loss of a large UK client at December 2025 contract expiry. The adjusted EBITDA remained barely positive at £0.1m (vs £0.8m H1 FY25) — a testament to aggressive cost management but also a signal of how thin the financial cushion is.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, the H1 tracking signal is the focus — but without FY1 consensus (no brokers covering), both revenue and EPS are UNTRACKABLE. The going concern disclosure is the dominant signal: directors have explicitly stated there are "material uncertainties which may cast significant doubt over the Group's ability to continue as a going concern." Cash at £0.9m, post-period outflows continuing, no debt facility secured, CFO departing end of April — the standalone operational trajectory is towards insolvency. The upgrade resilience is nil in the fundamental sense; the only resilience factor is the takeover offer. If the offer lapses, emergency equity or debt funding would be required within weeks. The gross margin improvement to 63% (from 59%) is a genuine structural positive from the Cloud product wind-down, but this matters only if the company survives as an independent entity.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: There are no meaningful broker revisions to model — coverage has been effectively suspended given the takeover. The sole relevant trading event is the 8 May 2026 unconditional deadline. If the offer becomes unconditional, shareholders receive 17p and the analysis ends. If the offer lapses, the company faces an acute cash crisis and the stock would likely collapse well below current levels. No TP assessment is appropriate. For the record: the standalone fundamental implies revenue continuing to contract toward £14–16m for FY26, EBITDA approaching zero in H2, and a capital raise requirement within 6–12 months.

🏁 H1 FY26 revenue −25%, ARR −24%, cash £0.9m, going concern disclosed — the standalone business is not viable. Recommended takeover at 17p is the only relevant outcome. Score 12/100 reflects fundamental position; offer provides the exit.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The most striking number in this RNS is the EBITDA margin of 34.9% (vs 29.7% FY24) — a 520bps improvement on the back of +61% EBITDA growth to EGP 2,738m. Revenue beat consensus by +1.5% at EGP 7,855m (+37% YoY), with gross margin expanding to 42.7% (from 38.1%). This is operationally a strong result. However, the definitive catalyst for broker action is the adjusted EPS of EGP 217p — a miss of −7.2% vs the pre-results consensus of 234p driven by a 39% effective tax rate (vs 30% in FY24). The FY24 30% rate was artificially depressed by EGP 303m FX gains that created a high non-taxable income base; FY25's 39% is the normalised rate and represents a structural earnings headwind that consensus had not fully priced.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, the key signal is the H1 FY26 tracking setup for the next event. The seasonal H1 baseline for FY26 is EGP 4,405m revenue (47.8% of £9,216m consensus); buy trigger at EGP 4,471m. EPS H1 FY26 baseline EGP 150.7p (buy trigger 153.1p). The strong FY25 H2 (~+33% YoY revenue growth) provides a high base; FY26 growth will naturally moderate from +37% toward +17% consensus. This deceleration is already embedded in FY26 consensus — but the tax rate recalibration means those FY26 estimates are likely too high. The downside is that once brokers reset to a 39% tax rate, FY26 EPS consensus could fall from 292p to the 235–265p range — a cut of 10–20%. The Elliott acquisition introduces strategic optionality but also uncertainty about FY26 cost structure or capital allocation shifts. Geopolitical risk to Jordan (13% of revenues) is the residual operational risk that could impair otherwise solid FY26 revenue progression.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY25 EPS will be revised down to ~EGP 217p adjusted (−7% from 234p). FY26 EPS consensus of 292p faces a more material cut of −10 to −20% once the 39% tax rate is incorporated — implying revised FY26 consensus in the 235–265p range. Revenue for FY26 may see modest upgrades (+2–3%) given branch rollout momentum. TP cuts probable — from current 75¢ consensus to perhaps 65–70¢ range. The primary watch point is whether brokers model the 39% tax rate as permanent (likely yes, per RNS explanation) or as cyclical (unlikely). Secondary watch point: Elliott's intentions and any announcement of a strategic review or capital returns policy change.

🏁 Operationally exceptional FY25 with EBITDA +61% and revenue +37%, but the 39% tax rate (vs 30% prior year) creates a structural EPS miss of −7% vs consensus and puts FY26 estimates — currently 292p — materially at risk of a 10–20% downgrade. Score 42/100.

The watch point is the full year results announcement (date not disclosed in this RNS) which will reveal PAM acquisition terms, consideration, synergy assumptions, and restated revenue trajectory.   • CEO departure: John-Paul Savant stepping down after 10+ years. This is a significant leadership change at a company in the middle of an acquisition integration. Brokers will flag this as a near-term uncertainty.
  • Chairish integration: Synergies $8m annual run rate by FY27 on track. But H1 EBITDA margin diluted by Chairish mix. First full year consolidation.
  • Revenue H1-weighting: Company explicitly guided "revenue growth more weighted to the first half." This implies H2 will be relatively softer. Brokers have this in their models.
  • Cost savings programme: "Additional modest cost savings programme... will benefit margins in FY27, with a small benefit in H2 26." 🏗️ Minor positive FY27 tailwind but not quantified — moderate signal.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

ATG · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

#1 Driver — FY26 guidance confirmation in-line: H1 revenue at c.$125m confirms the existing consensus midpoint almost exactly ($125.2m seasonal baseline). Brokers will hold FY26 estimates flat. The "in-line" confirmation removes downside risk but provides no upside catalyst.

#2 Driver — CEO departure: John-Paul Savant's resignation is the single most disruptive element of this RNS. After 10+ years as CEO through acquisitions including Chairish, his departure introduces strategic and execution uncertainty. Brokers may add a discount to target prices or apply a higher risk premium, even if estimates remain unchanged.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue (FY26e): Hold. $125m H1 in-line with consensus. No change.
  • FY1 EPS (FY26e): Hold. EBITDA in-line. No EPS revision expected. 38.7¢ unchanged.
  • FY2 Revenue (FY27e): Minor positive nudge from cost savings programme. +0–2%.
  • FY2 EPS (FY27e): Modest positive from FY27 cost savings + lower interest. +1–3%.
  • Target price: Brokers likely to trim TPs given CEO risk. Current consensus TP £5.08 vs share price 384p. Market already trades at significant discount. TP cuts likely to £4.80–5.00.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with market expectations" — no upside surprise. Does not trigger upgrade cycle.

Key risk: CEO departure coming during first full year of Chairish integration. Transition risk is high. Combined with I&C revenue declining, a flat organic H1 (pro forma cc +8% ahead of 4–5% guidance but H1-weighted was expected), the upside is limited and the leadership change is a genuine near-term negative.

Net FY1 EPS revision: hold. Consistency check: Tone must be Neutral. ✅

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

ATG · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

46/100 · Confidence: 40–52 · No FX adjustment · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

ComponentPts
🟢 FY26 guidance confirmed in-line — no downside risk to consensus+8
🟢 H1 revenue c.$125m — in-line with seasonal baseline ($125.2m)+5
🟢 Net debt/EBITDA declining to 1.8x — deleveraging on track+5
🟢 Chairish synergies on track ($8m run rate by FY27)+4

🔴 Share price de-rated -63% vs EPS period — market signalling structural concerns not visible in consensus−5

Total: 46/100

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The H1 FY26 trading update confirms revenue of approximately $125m, virtually in line with the seasonal baseline of $125.2m (3-year H1 average 51.6% × FY26e $242.7m). Pro forma constant currency growth of close to 8% comfortably exceeds the full-year guidance of 4–5%, providing confidence that first-half momentum is tracking above the full-year trend. However, the RNS simultaneously confirms that revenue weighting is H1-heavy by design, meaning the H2 run-rate will be relatively softer. The headline "FY26 guidance confirmed" is therefore holding, not upgrading — removing downside but creating no upside.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H1 revenue in-line means implied H2 of ~$117.7m is set against a FY26e consensus of $242.7m. On a pro forma basis this represents a slight YoY decline vs the comparable H2 FY25 (~$125m pro forma), consistent with company guidance of H1-weighted growth. The EBITDA margin is expected to reflect Chairish dilution as previously communicated. No H1 EPS disclosed, so the deviation signal is revenue-only at −0.1pp — IN LINE. The deliberate cost savings programme provides a modest FY27 tailwind (+1–3% EPS potential) but is not quantified. The balance sheet is deleveraging ahead of schedule (1.8x by end of H1 vs 2.0x Dec 25) — a quiet positive.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e estimates are likely to be held across revenue, EBITDA, and EPS. The FY27 cost savings programme provides a small positive nudge to forward estimates (+1–3%). Target prices are expected to be trimmed slightly to £4.80–5.00 (from £5.08 consensus) in response to the CEO departure, introducing a leadership risk premium even as financial delivery is on track. The CEO transition is the dominant narrative in broker notes — the financials are in-line but the execution risk during Chairish integration is elevated without a named successor. FY26 remains a transition year with organic EPS virtually flat.

🏁 ATG delivers an in-line H1 but the CEO departure headline overshadows confirmation of guidance, making this a hold rather than an upgrade catalyst. Score: 46/100.

Key insight: This is a retrospective full-year results RNS. The FX headwind was already embedded in the delivered FY25 number (£149.6m). PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

Option repricing (4.4m options at £6.45) adds incremental SBP charge FY26. Share count creep. Net FY1 EPS revision: upgrade (+6.9% on FY25 actual; FY26e major upgrade). Consistency check: Tone Constructive or Strongly positive. FY25 beat is solid; FY26e upgrade magnitude is large. But "Constructive" is appropriate given qualitative FY26 guidance and contingent consideration overhang. ✅

(Not Strongly positive — the FY26e upgrade will be large in absolute terms but the market is already de-rated, contingent consideration is a drag, and FY26 guidance is qualitative only. The broker upgrade cycle is clear but not "trigger-happy" as with an explicit numerical beat-and-raise.)

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

ELIX · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

72/100 − 5 (FX) = 67/100 · Confidence: 62–72 · FX Rule 1 applied (−5 pts) · 63% USD · 🟡 neutral rate · 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

🔴 FY26e consensus massively stale — upgrade magnitude hard to pin down cleanly−3

Final: 67/100

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The FY25 results deliver a clean earnings beat: adjusted diluted EPS of 58.7p exceeds the pre-RNS consensus of 54.9p by +3.8p (+6.9%). Revenue of £149.6m (+34% YoY) beats £149.0m consensus marginally; the quality is in the earnings line — EBITDA of £44.3m (+42% YoY, +2.3% vs Sharescope fc) and margin expansion of +1.6pp to 29.6% demonstrate operating leverage. The most significant forward signal is AI-related revenue up >260% YoY and TRC performing ahead of acquisition case — establishing the platform for a large FY26e upgrade.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Pre-FY mode. H2 FY25 revenue of £78.2m represents +76.5% YoY versus FY24's £44.3m, substantially acquisition-enhanced (TRC from Sep 2025). The H1 seasonality at 47.7% of FY total was almost exactly in-line with the 47.5% 3-year average. The key upgrade catalyst is not the FY25 result but the FY26e stale consensus: at 64.9p, it fails to capture TRC's full-year annualisation (~+13p on EPS bridge), Kvadrant's contribution (~+3–4p), and organic growth at maintained margin. The EPS bridge points to ~80–83p FY26e, representing a +20–30% upgrade that brokers must now execute. The only meaningful downside risk is GBP/USD remaining elevated into FY26, which limits the USD revenue translation benefit — but current spot is approximately neutral vs FY25 average.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY25 actual EPS confirmed at 58.7p (+6.9% vs consensus). FY26e revenue will be upgraded from £185.6m to approximately £200–220m (+8–18%). FY26e EPS will be upgraded from the stale 64.9p to ~78–85p (+20–31%) — the largest percentage EPS revision in this session. Target prices may move toward £9.50–11.50 though the current share price at 710p already trades at a significant discount to the £11.20 consensus TP. The primary constraint is the contingent consideration overhang (TRC up to £47.8m over FY26–28) and incremental SBP charges from option repricing, both of which dilute the shareholder return from otherwise strong earnings growth.

🏁 ELIX delivers a clean FY25 EPS beat and triggers one of the largest FY26e consensus upgrades in this batch as TRC's full-year annualisation is properly modelled — but the de-rated share price and contingent consideration overhang limit the upgrade cycle's clean expression. Score: 67/100.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The defining catalyst is the explicit full-year upgrade. Q1 2026 revenue of $242.1m is up +18% YoY and +24% QoQ, representing the strongest quarterly trading in recent years and establishing a base that makes the existing FY26 consensus of $780.8m clearly too low. Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Pre-H1 mode applies — H1 actuals pending. However, the Group's structural shift toward higher-value customers and US diversification provides a genuine revenue floor. The $16m incremental acquisition investment is deliberate growth capex — returning in cohort value over subsequent quarters — not a structural impairment.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will upgrade FY26e revenue by +5–10% to approximately $820–860m, and FY26e EPS by +5–8% to approximately 415–430¢ (vs stale 396.8¢). FY27e receives a secondary lift of +3–6% to ~435–450¢. The primary watch point is Q2 EBITDA given deliberately elevated acquisition spending; if margin stays compressed in Q2, some brokers may trim the EBITDA upgrade. The EPS upgrade is principally revenue-driven and remains robust even at flat margin.

🏁 PLUS is a clear pre-H1 upgrade play with explicit "ahead of expectations" language, Q1 five-year record Customer Income, and an accelerating EPS trajectory. Score: 76/100.

RSW

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY upgrade trading statement accordingly. Next year end = 30/6/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Year label mappings:

  • FY23 = 3y ago · FY24 = 2y ago · FY25 = 1y ago · FY26e = FY1 (1y fc) · FY27e = FY2 (2y fc)

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

RSW · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

  • Routing: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update with explicit guidance upgrade.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 156.5p · Revenue £759.3m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 174.6p · Revenue £801.9m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full period +19.8% (130.6p → 156.5p). Significant step-up in Sep 25 (large revision; +24.6p event). Revenue: £711.8m → £759.3m (+6.7%). 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (157.2p → 156.5p — slight drift, likely pre-announcement caution).

⚠️ Sharescope glitch confirmed: RSW data shows FY24: H1 61.7p / H2 133.2p → FY = 133.2p. H1+H2 = 61.7+133.2 = 194.9p ≠ stated FY 133.2p. The H2 field = FY field — classic Sharescope H2 corrupt = FY glitch. ⚠️ Deriving H2 as FY minus H1: FY24 H2 = 133.2p − 61.7p = 71.5p. This should be used throughout.

  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 48.7% of FY = £370.0m · EPS 43.8% of FY = 68.6p

⚠️ EPS H1 baseline correction needed: 3yr avg H1 EPS% uses FY23, FY24, FY25. FY24 H2 = 71.5p (corrected). FY23 H1 = 83.4p / FY23 = 155.1p = 53.8%. FY24 H1 = 61.7p / 133.2p = 46.3%. FY25 H1 = 63.2p / 137.8p = 45.9%. 3yr avg = (53.8+46.3+45.9)/3 = 48.7%. Sharescope H1 avg 43.8% may use different denominators — using my calculation: 48.7%. Revenue: FY23 H1 347.7/688.6=50.5%, FY24 330.5/691.3=47.8%, FY25 341.4/713.0=47.9% → 3yr avg 48.7% ✓

  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £341.4m · EPS 63.2p
  • H2 implied (pre-RNS): H1 FY26 actual = £365.6m. H2 pre-RNS = £759.3m − £365.6m = £393.7m vs FY25 H2 = £713.0m − £341.4m = £371.6m → +5.9% YoY. EPS: 156.5p − 68.8p = 87.7p vs FY25 H2 = 137.8p − 63.2p = 74.6p → +17.6% YoY.
  • FX: Currency = GBP. Renishaw has significant international revenues. No explicit currency section in this trading statement. Will assess in Phase 0B.
  • Phase 0B: RSW is a global manufacturer with significant overseas revenues in USD, EUR, JPY, etc. However the trading statement does not provide a currency movements section. From context, RSW discloses constant currency data when significant. The RNS says "we are actively managing the challenges and increasing costs imposed by ongoing economic and geopolitical uncertainties" — no specific FX guidance. No >30% single currency explicitly disclosed. Given no currency movements data, and the RNS is very short (numerical guidance only), applying missing baseline fallback: mid-point penalty if exposure >30% — but without confirmation of dominant currency, skip Phase 0B and note: FX exposure likely present but unquantifiable from this RNS. No FX badge applied.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net cash: FY26 H1 −£63.4m. FY1fc −£276.3m. FY2fc −£313.5m. This is a massive step-up in net cash from H1 £63.4m to FY1fc £276.3m — unusual, likely Sharescope fc includes anticipated dividend/capex. ND/EBITDA: FY1fc −1.70x (net cash). ND/FCF: −4.6x FY26. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RSW · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Trading Statement — Upgrade to FY2026 guidance, 20 April 2026)

  1. Revenue — FY26 guidance range: £775m to £805m. vs stale consensus £759.3m.
  • Range midpoint = £790m → beat vs consensus +£30.7m = +4.0%
  • Range floor = £775m → beat vs consensus +£15.7m = +2.1%
  • Range ceiling = £805m → beat vs consensus +£45.7m = +6.0%

"We now expect to deliver FY2026 full-year performance in the following ranges: Revenue: £775m to £805m"

  1. Adjusted PBT — FY26 guidance range: £145m to £165m. vs stale consensus £145.0m (Sharescope FY1fc PBT).
  • Range floor £145m = in-line with consensus
  • Range ceiling £165m = +£20m = +13.8% above consensus
  • Midpoint £155m = +6.9% above consensus

"Adjusted profit before tax: £145m to £165m"

  1. EPS bridge (FY27e):
  • New base: FY26 actual (to be reported). PBT midpoint £155m. Tax ~25% → PAT ~£116.3m. Diluted shares ~72.7m → adj EPS = ~160p (midpoint). Range: 150–170p.
  • If PBT top of range £165m → EPS ~170p vs stale FY26e 156.5p = +8.6%.
  • Organic growth delta FY27: Strong order book expansion. "Particularly strong demand from semiconductor, electronics manufacturing, aerospace & defence." These are multi-quarter cycles — FY27 revenue supported.
  • Interest step-up: Net cash growing from £63.4m H1 to ~£276m FY1fc. No interest cost issue.
  • FY27e EPS bridge: FY26 upgraded to ~155–170p. FY27e currently 174.6p. On a higher FY26 base, FY27e should upgrade to ~180–190p (+3–8% vs stale 174.6p).
  • Implied FY27e EPS: ~180–190p, representing +3–8% revision vs stale 174.6p.
  1. Demand drivers: "Particularly strong demand from semiconductor and electronics manufacturing equipment, and aerospace & defence sectors, with a further substantial expansion of our order book." Three positive signals: strong sector demand + order book expansion.

"Since our H1 results announcement on 11 February, we have seen particularly strong demand from customers in the semiconductor and electronics manufacturing equipment, and aerospace & defence sectors, with a further substantial expansion of our order book."

  1. Challenges / costs: "Actively managing the challenges and increasing costs imposed by ongoing economic and geopolitical uncertainties and supply chain pressures." This is an explicit caution on cost side — mitigating the upgrade language.

"We are actively managing the challenges and increasing costs imposed by ongoing economic and geopolitical uncertainties and supply chain pressures."

  1. Revenue update pending: "We will provide an update on our revenue performance to 31 March 2026, as planned, on 6 May 2026." This means the £365.6m H1 figure (from Sharescope) is confirmed; H1 was reported Feb 2026. The May 2026 update will be for the quarter to March (Q3 FY26).

EPS quality check: PBT range guidance £145–165m. Stale consensus £145m is at the floor. No non-recurring items flagged. "Adjusted" PBT — standard measure. Tax rate: ~25% consistent. No quality concerns — the upgrade is organic demand-driven. ✓

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification: The RNS is purely a guidance upgrade — no qualitative forward statements about FY27. The FY26 guidance upgrade is very explicit: revenue £775–805m vs £759.3m stale consensus, PBT £145–165m vs £145m consensus (floor to top = in-line to significant beat).

"Upgrade to FY2026 guidance" is the headline. This is 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering for FY26:

  • "We now expect to deliver FY2026 full-year performance in the following ranges" — explicit guidance raise
  • Both revenue and PBT ranges published
  • Covers FY26 only (no FY27 language beyond order book mention)
  • Divergence: No — H1 was already ahead and trajectory continues. ✅

Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering (+12 to +15 pts)

Note: As this is explicitly titled "Upgrade to FY2026 guidance" — this is the most unambiguous classification available.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

RSW · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

3.1 Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 cross-check (mandatory — glitch detected):

  • FY24: H1 £330.5m + corrected H2 £360.8m = £691.3m ✓ (matches FY field 691.3)
  • FY24 EPS: H1 61.7p + corrected H2 71.5p = 133.2p ✓
  • FY25: H1 £341.4m + H2 £371.6m = £713.0m ✓. EPS: 63.2p + 74.6p = 137.8p ✓
  • FY26 H1 actual: £365.6m. Using midpoint £790m for FY26 implied full year: H2 = £790m − £365.6m = £424.4m.
