Revenue trajectory: FY24 +0.4%, FY25 +3.1%, FY26 ~+10.8% → 🟢 Accelerating (strong surge from flat prior years) EPS trajectory: FY24 −14.1%, FY25 +3.5%, FY26 ~+16% → 🟢 Accelerating (recovering from FY24 trough)

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: RNS midpoint £790m → +10.8% vs prior +3.1% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived)
  • EPS: Midpoint ~160p → +16% vs prior +3.5% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived)

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-FY mode — write but do not score)

H1 FY26 actual = £365.6m. FY26 guidance midpoint £790m. H1 as % of FY26 = £365.6m / £790m = 46.3% vs 3yr avg 48.7% → deviation = −2.4pp

Signal (informational): 🔴 CAUTION (−1.5 to −3pp). H1 slightly below seasonal norm — but RNS has upgraded FY guidance, meaning H2 must be stronger. This is consistent with the strong demand acceleration noted post-H1 results.

EPS H1 tracking (informational): H1 EPS 68.8p / FY26e 156.5p = 44.0% vs 48.7% → deviation = −4.7pp. Below seasonal norm. But: FY26 EPS will upgrade from 156.5p to ~160p. Recalculated: 68.8p / 160p = 43.0% → deviation = −5.7pp. H1 EPS below seasonal, H2 must compensate.

Phase 3.2 not scored (pre-FY mode). Column 5: na.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — scored in Phase 5)

H2 base figure (RNS-derived midpoint): FY26 midpoint £790m − H1 £365.6m = £424.4m H2 range: Floor £775m − £365.6m = £409.4m · Ceiling £805m − £365.6m = £439.4m Prior H2 FY25 = £371.6m H2 YoY: midpoint = (£424.4m − £371.6m) / £371.6m = +14.2%

Classification: 🟢 strong (+14.2% YoY, above +10% threshold). RNS-derived.

EPS H2: PBT midpoint £155m → FY26 EPS ~160p. H2 EPS = ~160p − 68.8p = ~91.2p vs FY25 H2 74.6p → +22.3% YoY. 🟢 strong.

Phase 3.3 scored row: pre-FY mode → included in Phase 5. 🟢 strong.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS net +19.8% over full period (130.6p → 156.5p). Very large step-up in Sep 25 (+24.6p — possibly post-FY25 results upgrade). Since then modest further upgrades. 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (very slightly, 157.2p → 156.5p — likely pre-announcement drift/caution). Post-RNS this trend will reverse sharply.
  • Divergence: Price rallied from £31.64 → £40.68 (+28.6%) alongside EPS +19.8% — broadly aligned, no major divergence. Both rising together.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

RNS-vs-forecast reconciliation: RNS confirms strong demand and order book expansion. No explicit cash figure in this statement. Sharescope FY1fc net borrowing = −£276.3m (very large net cash vs H1 current −£63.4m). This large H1-to-FY step in net cash (−£63.4m → −£276.3m) in Sharescope seems anomalous. Likely reflecting expected large H2 cash generation — RSW has historically strong H2 free cash flow, consistent with high H2 revenue weighting. No RNS cash disclosure to verify. Note gap as informational — cannot reconcile without RNS cash figure.

ND/EBITDA: FY1fc −1.70x (net cash, substantial). Interest cover: negative (net cash). ND/FCF −4.6x. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — Phase 5 silent.

Forecast year earnings check:

  • Step 1: FY1fc EPS 156.5p → upgrading to ~160p. FY25 actual 137.8p → growing +16%. Revenue £759.3m (consensus pre-RNS) → actual ~£790m > FY25 £713.0m → ✅✅ growing +10.8%.
  • Step 2: FY2fc EPS 174.6p > FY1fc 156.5p → ✅✅ growing +11.5%. Revenue £801.9m > £759.3m → ✅✅ growing. Post-upgrade FY27e likely further enhanced.

3.6 Structural / One-off Flags

  • Semiconductor and electronics demand surge: Structural demand driver — AI infrastructure buildout driving semiconductor equipment capex globally. Renishaw's precision measurement tools are directly in the supply chain. Not a one-off.
  • Aerospace & defence: UK/European defence spending step-up a multi-year structural tailwind.
  • Supply chain and cost pressures: Explicitly flagged by management — geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain costs are headwinds that partially offset the demand surge.
  • Order book expansion — "substantial": Strong signal for FY27 revenue visibility.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

RSW · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

#1 Driver — Explicit FY26 guidance upgrade: Revenue range £775–805m (+2–6% vs £759.3m consensus). PBT range £145–165m (floor to +14% vs £145m consensus). The headline "Upgrade to FY2026 guidance" is unambiguous. Brokers will upgrade FY26 estimates across the board.

#2 Driver — Order book expansion and sector demand: "Substantial expansion of our order book" in semiconductor/electronics and aerospace/defence. These are forward-looking revenue signals that support FY27 upgrades beyond the FY26 raise.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue (FY26e): Upgrade from £759.3m to midpoint ~£790m. +4.0%.
  • FY1 PBT (FY26e): Upgrade from £145.0m. Midpoint £155m = +6.9%. Brokers likely model toward midpoint-to-upper range.
  • FY1 EPS (FY26e): Upgrade from 156.5p to approximately 160–165p (+2–5%).
  • FY2 Revenue (FY27e): Upgrade, supported by order book. £801.9m → ~£820–840m. +2–5%.
  • FY2 EPS (FY27e): Upgrade from 174.6p to ~180–190p. +3–9%.
  • Target price: Current TP £40.03, share price £40.68. Price is already above TP — brokers have not caught up. Post-upgrade TPs likely move to £44–48. Re-rating potential.

Conservative guidance read-through: Range guidance with both metrics provided — not cautious language. Titled "Upgrade to FY2026 guidance" — no ambiguity.

Key risk: Supply chain pressures and cost inflation could compress the PBT range toward the £145m floor rather than the £155–165m midpoint-to-upper range. If the FX headwind materialises meaningfully (Renishaw has significant international revenue), net revenue in GBP could be impacted. The fact that price is already above TP suggests the market partially anticipates the upgrade — upside may be partially priced.

Net FY1 EPS revision: upgrade (+2–5%). Consistency check: Tone Constructive or Strongly positive. Given explicit "Upgrade" language with dual metric ranges → Strongly positive. ✅

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

RSW · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

77/100 · Confidence: 72–82 · No FX badge (no Phase 0B trigger from available data) · 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

ComponentPts
🟢 Explicit FY26 guidance upgrade — revenue £775–805m vs £759.3m consensus (+2–6%)+15
🟢 PBT upgrade range £145–165m — midpoint £155m = +6.9% vs £145m consensus+12
🟢 H2 FY26 implied revenue +14.2% YoY (midpoint) — H2 surge confirming demand acceleration+10
🟢 Semiconductor + aerospace/defence structural demand — order book "substantially expanded"+9
🟢 EPS trajectory accelerating — FY24 −14%, FY25 +3.5%, FY26 ~+16%+8
🟢 Net cash >£276m FY1fc — balance sheet supports further growth investment+5
🟡 Supply chain and cost pressures explicitly flagged — may compress toward PBT range floor−3
🟡 4-week EPS trend FALLING into announcement — partial pricing-in risk−2
🔴 PBT range floor (£145m) = in-line with stale consensus — downside risk if cost headwinds bite−5
🔴 FY27e revenue growth only +1.5% stale consensus — forward year growth slowdown−4
🔴 Share price already above consensus TP £40.03 (close £40.68) — market partially priced upgrade−3
🔴 H1 FY26 revenue at 46.3% of FY guidance midpoint — slightly below seasonal norm (H2 heavy)−2

Total: 77/100

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline says it all: "Upgrade to FY2026 guidance." Revenue guidance of £775m–£805m (midpoint £790m) is above the pre-RNS consensus of £759.3m by +4.0% at the midpoint, with the ceiling implying +6.0%. Adjusted PBT of £145m–£165m raises the earnings bar from the stale consensus floor of £145m to a midpoint of £155m, representing a +6.9% upgrade at mid-range. The underlying driver is crystal clear: "particularly strong demand from customers in the semiconductor and electronics manufacturing equipment, and aerospace & defence sectors" combined with a "further substantial expansion of our order book" — both structural tailwinds tied to AI infrastructure buildout and European defence spending escalation.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Pre-FY mode. H2 FY26 implied revenue at the midpoint is approximately £424m, representing +14.2% YoY versus FY25's £371.6m — the strongest H2 in the company's recent history. H2 EPS implied at approximately 91p versus FY25's 74.6p represents +22.3% YoY growth. The bear case rests on cost headwinds: management explicitly flags "increasing costs imposed by ongoing economic and geopolitical uncertainties and supply chain pressures" — if these compress margins toward the PBT floor of £145m, EPS remains flat vs stale consensus rather than upgrading. However, the order book expansion provides a buffer: even at the floor, revenue remains significantly above consensus.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e revenue will be upgraded from £759.3m to approximately £790m (+4.0%), and FY26e EPS from 156.5p to ~160–165p (+2–5%). FY27e receives a secondary lift to approximately £820–840m revenue and 180–190p EPS (+3–9%) supported by order book visibility. Target prices are expected to move to £44–48 from the stale £40.03 consensus — the current price at £40.68 is already through the old TP, creating a re-rating scenario. The primary watch point is cost management: brokers will focus on the PBT range width (£145–165m, a £20m spread) and whether supply chain disruptions push toward the floor.

🏁 RSW delivers an explicit, unambiguous FY26 guidance upgrade driven by structural semiconductor and defence demand, with strong H2 momentum and order book expansion underpinning a genuine upgrade cycle. Score: 77/100.

SUP

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update / FY guidance update accordingly. Next year end = 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Year label mappings:

  • FY23 = 3y ago · FY24 = 2y ago · FY25 = 1y ago · FY26e = FY1 (1y fc) · FY27e = FY2 (2y fc)

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

SUP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

  • Routing: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update accordingly.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 18.4p · Revenue £245.7m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 20.5p · Revenue £290.4m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full period −17.5% (22.3p → 18.4p). Material downgrade cycle in Jul 25 (22.3→17.9p, -4.4p event). Partial recovery Oct 25 (17.9→18.4p). Then flat from Oct 25 to Apr 26 — stalled at 18.4p for six months. Revenue: £235.1m → £245.7m (+4.5%). 4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 46.0% of FY = £113.1m · EPS 42.9% of FY = 7.9p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £113.0m · EPS 10.8p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): H1 FY26 actual = £132.6m (per Sharescope current H1). H2 implied = FY26e £245.7m − £132.6m = £113.1m. Prior H2 FY25 = £118.1m. Implied H2 YoY = £113.1m − £118.1m = −4.2%. EPS: FY26e 18.4p − H1 actual 8.8p = H2 implied 9.6p vs FY25 H2 = 10.2p → −5.9%
  • FX: Currency = GBP. No FX exposure. Phase 0B N/A.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: FY25 H2 £0.5m → FY26 H1 £19.9m (net debt) → FY1fc £7.3m → FY2fc £1.1m. ND/EBITDA FY1fc 0.20x. Interest cover 23.2x. ND/FCF 0.6x. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash (essentially).

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

SUP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (FY26 — twelve months ended 31 March 2026)

  1. Revenue — FY26 actual: "expects to report a 15% increase in FY26 revenues of c.£265.0 million (FY25: £231.1 million)." vs FY26e consensus £245.7m → beat of £19.3m = +7.9%.

"The Company expects to report a 15% increase in FY26 revenues of c.£265.0 million (FY25: £231.1 million)"

  1. EBITDA — FY26 actual: "Adjusted EBITDA of approximately £40.6 million (FY25: £40.5 million), significantly ahead of market consensus expectations." vs consensus £37.0m → beat of £3.6m = +9.7%. EBITDA margin: £40.6m/£265.0m = 15.3% vs FY25 £40.5m/£231.1m = 17.5%. Margin compression of 2.2pp despite revenue growth — driven by acquisition costs and investment in new facilities.

"Adjusted EBITDA of approximately £40.6 million (FY25: £40.5 million), significantly ahead of market consensus expectations"

  1. EPS bridge (FY27e):
  • New base: FY26 EBITDA £40.6m. Finance costs: net cash ~£7.3m FY26. Interest income likely positive. Capex £5.0m. Tax ~25%. Adj PBT ~ EBITDA − D&A − interest cost. Working: EBITDA £40.6m, D&A estimated ~£3–4m (from asset base), interest net ~nil, PBT ~£37m, tax ~£9.25m, PAT ~£27.75m, shares ~117.3m → EPS ~23.7p (basic). But wait — Sharescope FY26e EPS is only 18.4p on consensus, implying significant adjustments. The company uses "Adjusted EBITDA" which excludes share-based payments, fair value movements, exceptional items. Statutory EPS will be lower. Using 18.4p consensus as adjusted EPS benchmark.
  • EPS bridge: FY26 actual adj EBITDA = £40.6m vs consensus £37.0m → +£3.6m upside. FY27e drivers: SlimFast (acquired during FY26) full year contribution; new manufacturing facilities operational; vaping resilience continues. Vaping +10%+ despite ban confirms structural resilience.
  • Organic EBITDA growth: FY26 £40.6m achieved despite acquisitions of £12.4m (SlimFast etc.) and £5.0m capex. FY27 benefit from full-year SlimFast + margin normalisation as acquisition costs fall away.
  • 🏗️ Investment step-up: "investment in two brand new manufacturing facilities." New wellness facility 40,000 sq ft. RNS states "positioned for long-term growth" — cost timing in FY26/FY27. FY26 capex £5.0m confirmed (matches Sharescope fc). FY27 ongoing running costs from new facilities = mild negative. Score as FY+1 consideration.
  • FY27e EPS bridge: FY26 consensus 18.4p will upgrade to ~20–22p on EBITDA beat alone (+9.7%). FY27e 20.5p (current) will be revised to ~22–24p on SlimFast full year + margin recovery. Implied FY27e EPS upgrade +7–17% vs stale 20.5p.
  1. Vaping: "expected to be more than 10% higher than prior year even with the UK disposable vape ban on 1 June 2025." This directly addresses the key bear case — ban proved manageable. Demonstrates market resilience and category strength.

"Sales from the Group's Vaping category are expected to be more than 10% higher than prior year even with the UK disposable vape ban on 1 June 2025"

  1. Drinks & Wellness / SlimFast: "boosted by an excellent contribution from SlimFast." SlimFast acquired during FY26, no full-year contribution in FY26 → FY27 gets full year.
  2. Capital returns / Balance sheet: After £12.4m acquisitions + £5.0m capex, "the Group remains net-cash positive at 31 March 2026." Robust balance sheet. RNS-vs-forecast reconciliation: RNS net cash positive vs Sharescope FY1fc net debt £7.3m (positive = debt). RNS explicitly says net-cash positive — variance vs Sharescope.   • Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY26fc EBITDA £10.1m vs FY25 £6.1m = +£4.0m improvement guided. RNS CEO: "expect to deliver an improved financial performance in 2026, in line with market expectations." FY26fc EPS 44.8p = £8.3m PAT / 12.6m shares × tax = implies PBT ~£11.0m. From FY25 PBT £4.1m to FY26fc PBT implied ~£8.3m = +£4.2m improvement — driven by volume recovery, Yate closure cost savings, and higher productive hours already secured.
  • Interest step-up: nil (net cash).
  • FY26e implied: 44.8p consensus appears to be already reflecting the recovery. EPS bridge supports this — no new upgrade catalyst beyond confirmation that FY26 trajectory is intact. The beat on FY25 (27.1p vs 18.8p fc) is the relevant event today.
  1. Order book / forward work: "Strong and growing order book for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027." "Strong level of production hours secured for projects due to be delivered in 2026 and 2027." No specific order book value disclosed. Peter Marshall Steel Stairs: "strong order book for the current year and into 2027." SPC: "record year in 2025."

"The Group has a strong and growing order book for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027"

  1. Margin/cost signals: Underlying ROS: PBT £4.1m / Revenue £95.7m = 4.3% vs FY24 £10.8m/£113.1m = 9.5%. Yate facility closure (£2.8m non-underlying costs) — structural cost saving. Higher productive hours (+4.2%) vs lower revenue (−15.4%) reflects focus shift to complex, higher-margin projects with less steel content.
  2. Capital/balance sheet: Cash £20.5m (vs £21.7m FY24) — marginal reduction. Debt free. DPS 11.0p (vs 25.0p FY24) — 56% cut, covered 2.46× by underlying EPS.

"A dividend of 11.0 pence per share in respect of 2025 (25.0 pence per share paid in respect of 2024)"

  1. Qualitative tone FY26: "Entered 2026 with increased confidence and expect to deliver an improved financial performance in 2026, in line with market expectations." CEO points to order book visibility, improved cost base, and data centres/energy-from-waste market demand.

EPS quality check: Underlying EPS 27.1p vs basic EPS 10.4p — £2.8m non-underlying costs (Yate closure restructuring) excluded from underlying. This is appropriate and clean; £2.8m/12.6m = 2.4× difference correctly reflects the adjustments. The underlying figure is the operative metric for broker comparisons.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 guidance: "in line with market expectations" with positive tone ("increased confidence," growing order book). Yate closure costs are one-off (non-recurring in FY26). The step-up from FY25 underlying EPS 27.1p to FY26fc 44.8p is a +65% guided recovery — very large. Guidance does not explicitly upgrade beyond the 44.8p/£125m consensus.

Classification: 🟡 In-line with positive undertone (confirmed order book, cost base improved). Points: +1 to +3.

  • FY26 Revenue: £125m consensus likely held/trimmed slightly if demand recovery is gradual. Structural steel market remains competitive.
  • TP: Consensus 380p = current price 380p. Zero implied upside at TP. Brokers will almost certainly raise TP given the underlying EPS beat — new TP likely £420–460p range (+10–20%).

Post-revision, "in line with [new] expectations" will imply a higher actual outcome for FY26 if management maintains similar conservatism.

Key risk: FY24 was a peak year (£113.1m revenue, 66.2p EPS); the structural steel market has been in sustained demand decline with pricing pressure since. The Yate closure improves cost efficiency but doesn't resolve demand. FY26 revenue consensus of £125m (+30.5% from FY25 trough) assumes a significant market recovery — not guaranteed.

🔴 Dividend cut −56% (25p→11p) — signals board caution despite beat−3

Raw: +15+7+6+5+4−2−3−5−4−3−3 = +17 → 50 base + 17 = ~67 (green-low band)

Para 1 — Headline numbers: BILN delivered FY25 underlying EPS of 27.1p against consensus of 18.8p — a +44.1% beat — the dominant catalyst. Revenue of £95.7m also beat by +3.5% vs £92.5m. Underlying PBT of £4.1m (+17% beat) and EBITDA of £6.1m (+13% beat) confirm that the H2 trough anticipated by brokers was not as deep as feared. The Yate facility closure generated £2.8m of non-underlying costs which are excluded from the underlying basis — these are clean one-offs that will not recur. The statutory PBT of £1.3m vs underlying £4.1m confirms the nature of the charge.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, H2 FY25 revenue of £53.9m was −2.4% YoY (🟡 flat) and H2 EPS of 17.7p was −56.1% YoY (🔴 severe) — both confirming the challenging conditions management described. However, the context is critical: the FY25 underlying EPS of 27.1p massively exceeded the consensus of 18.8p that was set post the Oct 25 downgrade, meaning the H2 weakness was already over-discounted. The order book for FY26/FY27 is described as "strong and growing," with production hours secured in data centres and energy-from-waste — markets with resilient demand. The clean balance sheet (£20.5m cash, debt free) provides full flexibility for FY26 execution.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: The FY25 EPS upgrade from 18.8p → 27.1p (+44.1%) is the primary revision event. FY26 EPS likely held at 44.8p (management guided explicitly in-line), but this may prove conservative given the higher FY25 starting point — modest upside to 47–49p (+5–10%) if the order book converts as indicated. TP will almost certainly be raised from 380p — the current price equals the stale TP, which is now definitively too low given the underlying beat; new TP range likely £420–460p from Cavendish. The dividend cut to 11p (from 25p) confirms the board is not yet signalling full recovery — watch: FY26 H1 results for order book momentum and whether pricing pressure has eased.

🏁 A 44% underlying EPS beat vs consensus is a high-conviction buy signal for FY25; FY26 recovery trajectory is confirmed in-line; TP upgrades highly probable. Score 67/100.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

CRST · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/10/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (titled "Trading Update", issued 21 April 2026, covers period since 25 March AGM update)

1. Revenue / Volume — explicit guidance cut

Volume guidance cut to 1,400–1,500 units from prior guidance of 1,550–1,700 units — a reduction of 150–200 units at midpoint (~10% cut to the midpoint of 1,625 → 1,450).

"…reducing its volume expectations to 1,400 to 1,500 units (previously 1,550 to 1,700 units). The current order book for the financial year stands at 1,106 units."

Land sale revenue cut to c.£40m from prior guidance of £75–100m — a cut of £47.5m at midpoint (~55% reduction).

"The Group is now anticipating a reduced number of land sales, with expected revenue of c. £40m (previously £75m to £100m)."

"…the Group does not expect to make a material level of profit on disposals in the remainder of the financial year."

Combined effect vs FY26e consensus £620.7m: volume revenue impact at £250–270k ASP per unit × ~150 unit midpoint cut ≈ £37–40m; land revenue cut ≈ −£47.5m midpoint vs prior guidance. Total implied revenue miss vs pre-RNS consensus is likely £60–80m, putting FY26e revenue in the range of £540–560m — approximately 10–13% below prior consensus of £620.7m.

2. EPS / EBIT — explicit profit warning with guided range

EBIT guided to £5m–£15m with interest costs of c.£15m → implied PBT of £(10)m to £0m. This compares to prior consensus PBT of £35.6m — a cut of £36–46m or ~100–130% below prior consensus.

"As a result of these revised assumptions the Group now expects to achieve an EBIT for the financial year of around £5m to £15m, with interest costs of c. £15m and a revised year end net debt position of £100m to £120m."

Implied EPS: PBT of £(10)m to £0m → tax likely nil/minimal at these levels → EPS implied 0p to flat, vs prior FY26e consensus of 9.8p. This is a near-total consensus wipe-out.

FY26e EPS bridge (for Phase 4): New base = ~0–1p (FY26 actuals). For FY27e (FY2), organic recovery would need to be modelled from a dramatically lower base. With net debt guided £100–120m at year end (vs prior £44.9m fc), interest costs step up materially in FY27e as well. Prior FY27e consensus of 12.8p is substantially too high.

3. Order book / forward visibility

Order book 1,106 units against revised full-year target of 1,400–1,500. Coverage = 74–79% of revised target with roughly six months remaining to October year-end. Low visibility on new reservations in context of falling enquiries.

"The current order book for the financial year stands at 1,106 units."

"…there has been a reduction in new enquiries and visitor levels."

4. Balance sheet — covenant relaxation sought

Net debt at year end guided £100–120m vs prior fc £44.9m — a deterioration of £55–75m. Covenant relaxation being sought from lenders.

"…it is in the early stages of seeking temporary banking covenant relaxation. Discussions with the Group's lenders have commenced and a further update will be provided in due course."

This is a material balance sheet flag. ND/EBITDA on revised EBIT of £10m midpoint (EBITDA likely £20–30m including D&A) vs net debt £110m midpoint = ND/EBITDA ~4–5x. Interest cover at £10m EBIT midpoint / £15m interest = 0.67x — below 1x.

5. Cost pressures

Higher build costs flagged due to energy costs. No quantum given. NLW step-up also relevant (April 2026).

"Given the higher level of energy costs the Group has built in an expectation of higher build costs in the balance of the financial year."

6. Macro / demand tone

Macro deterioration cited: higher-for-longer interest rates, Middle East conflict, consumer confidence deterioration. Land market sentiment sharply softer.

"…macro-uncertainty has increased, with the ongoing conflict in the Middle East contributing to the prospect of a more prolonged higher interest rate environment, renewed cost pressures and a deterioration in consumer confidence."

"…there has been a marked softening in sentiment among prospective land purchasers. Buyers have become more cautious in the face of the uncertain outlook, resulting in reduced engagement in bidding processes and an increased reluctance to transact at market values."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

🔴🔴 Profit warning

Guidance phrase: "the Group now expects to achieve an EBIT for the financial year of around £5m to £15m" — numeric, explicit, covers FY26 only. Covenant relaxation sought.

Nature: fully numeric. Single year coverage (FY26). Mid-point EBIT £10m vs prior consensus PBT £35.6m = ~72% cut to pre-tax profit. EPS implied ~0–1p vs 9.8p consensus.

Provisional points: −12 to −15.

Divergence check: No divergence paradox — both current delivery and outlook are severely negative. The AGM statement (25 March) had apparently maintained prior guidance; this RNS represents a rapid deterioration within four weeks. Flag: this is a profit warning issued between AGM update and H1 results — the acceleration of macro deterioration since 25 March is the stated trigger.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

#2 Driver — Net debt deterioration and covenant relaxation Revised year-end net debt of £100–120m vs prior fc £44.9m is a £55–75m adverse swing. Target price and recommendation: Brokers will cut TPs substantially. Prior consensus TP £186p vs close 105.6p already reflected significant pessimism. The volume guidance range of 1,400–1,500 carries further downside risk given falling enquiries and the order book covers only 74–79% of the bottom end of that range.

Key risk: The covenant relaxation process is the single most significant risk beyond the earnings cut. "…it is in the early stages of seeking temporary banking covenant relaxation. Discussions with the Group's lenders have commenced and a further update will be provided in due course." If covenants are not relaxed on acceptable terms, the Group may face constraints on operations or be required to raise equity — materially dilutive. This is not priced with certainty at current levels.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The defining event in this RNS is an unambiguous profit warning: EBIT guided to £5–15m (midpoint £10m) for FY26, against interest costs of c.£15m — implying PBT of £(10)m to £0m versus a pre-RNS consensus PBT of £35.6m. This represents a ~100% cut to pre-tax consensus. The implied FY26 EPS collapses from 9.8p to approximately 0–1p. The #1 catalyst is the simultaneous volume cut (to 1,400–1,500 units from 1,550–1,700) and the near-total elimination of land sale profit (land revenue cut 55% to £40m, nil material profit on disposals). These are not soft caveats — they are explicit numeric guidance revisions issued less than four weeks after the AGM statement that apparently held prior guidance.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: There is no upgrade resilience case here. In pre-H1 mode, Phase 3.2 is untrackable for both metrics — no H1 FY26 actuals are disclosed — but the FY-level EBIT guidance makes the picture unambiguous. Implied H2 FY26 revenue is approximately £296m against an FY25 H2 of £353.3m — a YoY decline of ~−16%, classified as 🔴 severe. Implied H2 EPS is approximately 0p versus FY25 H2 of 5.5p. The H2 EBIT burden requires the second half to deliver the entirety of the £5–15m EBIT guided for the full year if H1 is broadly breakeven — and that is before interest. Meanwhile, build costs are rising (energy costs, April NLW), land buyers are withdrawing, new enquiries are falling, and the Group is in early-stage lender covenant discussions. The ⛔⛔ profit warning risk flag from Phase 3.3 is not prospective — it has crystallised. The only scenario where downside is contained is if macro conditions rapidly reverse in H2, which management explicitly does not expect ("likely to continue for at least the balance of its financial year").

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will cut FY26e EPS to approximately 0–1p (from 9.8p — a ~90–100% reduction) and FY26e revenue to approximately £540–560m (from £620.7m — ~10–13% cut). FY27e EPS will be cut from 12.8p to approximately 6–9p — the higher debt load entering FY27 (£100–120m vs £45m modelled) adds ~£3–4m incremental annual interest that alone strips 1–1.5p from FY27e EPS before any volume uncertainty is considered. Consensus TPs will be cut from the pre-RNS £186p to an estimated £80–120p range, with valuation migrating from earnings-based to NAV/book-based given near-zero FY26 earnings. At a current price of 105.6p, the stock is not obviously cheap even post-fall — NAV will have eroded given fire remediation provisions, lower land values, and the working capital drag from completed apartment inventory being fast-tracked to disposal. The covenant relaxation process is the principal watch point: if banking discussions extend or conditions prove onerous, equity issuance risk cannot be excluded, which would reset the per-share figures further. 🏁 Unambiguous profit warning — brokers will cut FY26 EPS by ~90%, FY27e by ~30–50%, and TP materially. Covenant risk adds dilution tail. Score: 8/100.

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results / pre-FY update accordingly. Next year end = 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

European and RoW sales represent £76.6m / £190.7m = 40.2% of total revenues. Multi-currency (EUR, SEK, others). No single non-GBP currency >30% broken out individually. The RNS does not disclose a Currency Movements table with specific rates. Without a single currency >30%, Phase 0B does not formally trigger. N/A — but note European revenue mix noted as context.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 31.8p · Revenue £186.3m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 20.7p · Revenue £200.2m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change +488.9% (5.4p → 31.8p) over full period — massive upgrade cycle across the snapshot. Multiple step-ups. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT (stable at 31.8p since Jan 26). Revenue: +27.1% (£146.7m → £186.3m).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 43.0% of FY = £80.1m · EPS n/a (H1 historically loss-making, meaningless baseline).
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £61.7m · EPS −5.9p
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY26fc £186.3m − H1 £80.7m = H2 £105.6m vs FY25 H2 £85.0m → +24.2% YoY. EPS: FY26fc 31.8p − H1 9.1p = H2 22.7p vs FY25 H2 9.7p → +134% YoY.
  • FX: N/A as above.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: FY23 −£7.7m nc → FY24 −£11.7m nc → FY25 −£8.9m nc → H1 FY26 +£22.9m → FY26fc +£1.2m → FY27fc +£7.2m. Significant swing: H1 FY26 net debt £22.9m but FY26fc only £1.2m — expected major cash generation H2. ND/EBITDA FY26fc 0.07x — essentially zero. Interest cover FY26fc 7.8x. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered at year-end. Note: H1 was temporarily leveraged (warehouse deposits/seasonality).

Investment step-up rule — mandatory check: RNS discloses: "new UK warehouse" lease completed 1 April 2026; warehouse fit-out "total fit-out costs for FY27 are expected to be £10.2m." This is a FY27 cost event — timing falls in FY27. Trigger confirmed: FY2 investment step-up. Mandatory scored negative in Phase 5 at −3 to −6 pts.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

G4M · Q2 · Full Year Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Full Year Trading Update

The company explicitly discloses pre-RNS consensus in the footnote: revenue £186.4m, EBITDA £17.7m, PBT £9.3m. This is the authoritative consensus baseline.

  1. Revenue — FY26 actual: £190.7m vs pre-RNS consensus £186.4m = +£4.3m / +2.3% beat. vs FY25 £146.7m = +30.0% YoY. UK sales £114.1m (+26% YoY); European/RoW £76.6m (+36% YoY).

"Total sales: £190.7m (FY25: £146.7m), +30%"

  1. EPS / earnings — FY26: PBT "not less than £9.7m" vs consensus £9.3m = +£0.4m / +4.3% beat (floor). EBITDA "not less than £18.1m" vs consensus £17.7m = +£0.4m / +2.3% beat (floor). Gross margin 28.4% vs FY25 27.0% = +1.4pp expansion. No EPS figure yet — formal prelims 23 June 2026. EPS bridge: PBT ≥£9.7m × ~75% tax / 21.0m shares = ≥34.6p vs FY26fc 31.8p = ≥+8.8% beat (floor calculation).

"EBITDA to be not less than £18.1m (FY25: £10.0m)" "Profit before tax to be not less than £9.7m (FY25: £1.6m)"

FY27e EPS bridge:

  • New base: FY26 adj PBT ≥£9.7m, implied EPS ≥34.6p
  • Inorganic annualisation delta: nil (organic growth)
  • Organic EBITDA growth delta: pre-RNS FY27fc EBITDA £16.0m vs FY26 ≥£18.1m — FY27fc EBITDA is already BELOW FY26 actual by ≥−£2.1m. This is because the new warehouse fit-out costs of £10.2m capex (FY27) will generate significantly higher D&A (warehouse lease D&A) and potentially higher rent. Company explicitly states FY27 trading "in line with market expectations" — and the disclosed FY27 consensus PBT is £6.0m vs FY26 ≥£9.7m (a massive implied step-DOWN).
  • Interest step-up delta: Net debt FY27fc £7.2m — marginal interest cost. Not the main driver.
  • FY27e implied: FY27fc PBT £6.0m vs FY26 ≥£9.7m = −38.1% decline in PBT. EPS: £6.0m × 75% / 21.0m = 21.4p vs FY27fc 20.7p — consensus already models this correctly. The warehouse step-up is already in the numbers.

⚠️ Critical observation: FY27 consensus EPS (20.7p) is already BELOW FY26 implied EPS (≥34.6p). This is the defining feature of this RNS. The FY26 beat is real but does not drive FY27 upgrades — the market already knew FY27 EBITDA would drop due to the warehouse investment cycle.

  1. Forward work / FY27 outlook: "FY27 trading to date in line with market expectations." Revenue growth "continued into April 2026." No upgrade language for FY27. Company explicitly flags FY27 consensus (revenue £200.2m, EBITDA £16.0m, PBT £6.0m).

"FY27 trading to date in line with market expectations"

  1. Gross margin: 28.4% vs 27.0% FY25 and 27.3% FY24 — progressive improvement. Significant driver of EBITDA performance alongside revenue growth.
  2. Capital / balance sheet: Net bank debt £5.0m at 31 March 2026 vs £6.4m at March 2025 — further reduced despite £3.6m warehouse deposit paid in Q4 FY26. Debt-free excluding minor net bank debt.
  3. Technical/AI development: AI inventory forecasting platform, digital promotions centre, website AI chatbot — described as "already supporting further growth." Qualitative only.

EPS quality check: No tax rate distortion visible. Underlying vs reported basis not differentiated in this update.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY27 guidance: "in line with market expectations" — confirming the already-known FY27 EBITDA step-down (£16.0m vs £18.1m FY26). No upgrade language. The company explicitly confirms FY27 consensus as-is.

Investment step-up rule fires: The warehouse fit-out cost of £10.2m (FY27 timing confirmed) is a mandatory negative. FY27 EBITDA step-down already in consensus numbers — so this doesn't create a new downgrade, but it confirms no upgrade.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — FY27 confirmed at consensus; no upgrade language; warehouse investment cycle acknowledged. Points: 0 to +3.

Divergence check: FY26 material beat (+30% revenue, +2.3% vs consensus) → FY27 in-line/flat. 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery. FY26 outperformance does not translate to FY27 upgrades due to the warehouse investment overhang.

  • EPS trend: +488.9% net change — remarkable upgrade cycle across the year. 5.4p → 31.8p through multiple step-ups (June 25: 5.4→10.2, Sept: 10.2→11.6, Oct: 11.6→18.6, Nov: 18.6→23.1, Dec: 23.1→25.7, Jan 26: 25.7→31.8). Consistent re-rating as H1 FY26 results confirmed turnaround.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT (stable since Jan 26 at 31.8p)
  • Divergence: Price has tracked consensus upgrades (245p → 415p) — fully correlated.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Step 2: FY27fc EPS 20.7p < FY26 implied ≥34.6p → 🚨 FY27fc EPS −40.2% below FY26. 🚨 FY27fc Revenue £200.2m > FY26 £190.7m ✅. Note: EPS decline fully explained by warehouse investment step-up — ⚠️ replace 🚨 with ⚠️ (known one-off investment cost in comparison year).

3.6 Structural Flags

Warehouse investment cycle (FY27 impact): The new UK warehouse (lease commenced 1 April 2026, fit-out £10.2m capex in FY27) will generate: additional D&A (capex £10.2m over say 10 years = ~£1.0m extra D&A FY27); IFRS 16 lease liability (new lease); potential temporary dual-running costs during transition. Management previously guided FY27 PBT £6.0m vs FY26 ≥£9.7m — the step-down is well-flagged.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

G4M · Q2 · Full Year Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

#1 Driver — FY26 revenue £190.7m and EBITDA ≥£18.1m vs consensus (both beats): Revenue +2.3% beat and EBITDA +2.3% beat on a consensus that itself was recently upgraded to 31.8p. This confirms the turnaround at the highest level and will prompt brokers to upgrade FY26 formal EPS. The gross margin expansion to 28.4% (+1.4pp) is an additional quality signal.

#2 Driver — FY27 in-line with depressed consensus (PBT £6.0m, warehouse drag): The dominant FY27 narrative is negative — management explicitly confirms FY27 consensus which models PBT of £6.0m vs FY26 ≥£9.7m. This is a known, pre-flagged step-down but it will prevent any FY27 EPS upgrades today. The investment step-up rule fires.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26 EPS: Current consensus 31.8p. Actual implied ≥34.6p (floor from PBT ≥£9.7m). Formal EPS on 23 June. Brokers likely to upgrade FY26 EPS to ~34–36p range (+7–13%).
  • FY27 EPS: Confirmed in-line with 20.7p consensus. Hold at 20.7p. The warehouse fit-out absorbs all profit momentum. No upgrade expected.
  • FY27 Revenue: £200.2m consensus confirmed in-line. Hold.
  • TP: Consensus 415p. Current price 245p = 69% discount to TP. Given FY26 beat, brokers likely to maintain or modestly raise TP toward 430–450p for prelims in June. The FY27 drag limits the re-rating multiple.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Not less than" language on EBITDA and PBT is floor guidance — floor PBT ≥£9.7m vs consensus £9.3m. The actual figure (disclosed June) may exceed £9.7m. Formal prelims on 23 June 2026 are the real event.

Key risk: FY27 warehouse transition. If the new warehouse integration takes longer or runs over budget (£10.2m fit-out), FY27 PBT risk is to the downside. Additionally, European revenue was +36% YoY — if macro headwinds (tariffs, consumer confidence) hit European markets in FY27, the implied recovery trajectory is challenged.

Consistency check: Net FY26 EPS revision: upgrade (+7–13%). FY27: hold. Overall tone: Constructive (upgrade on current year, hold on forward).

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely — strong FY26 beat drives immediate EPS upgrades; FY27 already models the warehouse step-down correctly; catalysts limited to FY26 formal confirmation in June.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: G4M delivered FY26 revenue of £190.7m against pre-RNS consensus £186.4m — a +2.3% beat — and FY26 EBITDA of "not less than £18.1m" vs consensus £17.7m (+2.3% floor beat). Gross margin expanded to 28.4% from 27.0% FY25 — a third consecutive year of improvement. Most critically, PBT "not less than £9.7m" vs consensus £9.3m (+4.3% floor), implying FY26 EPS of ≥34.6p vs current consensus 31.8p (+9% minimum). The turnaround story is complete on FY26 — revenue grew +30% YoY in a single year with UK +26% and Europe +36%.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY26 revenue of £110.0m (+29.4% YoY) confirms the acceleration was not first-half skewed — momentum sustained through year-end. Gross margin expansion and disciplined cost control have driven EBITDA growth of ≥+81% YoY (£10.0m → ≥£18.1m). Revenue tracking deviation in pre-FY mode was 🟡 IN LINE (−0.7pp) — no seasonal distortion. The upgrade resilience case is straightforward: even at the floor, FY26 beats consensus. The only downside risk is that the formal EPS figure (23 June) reveals one-off items or a tax rate deviation, but the PBT floor of ≥£9.7m anchors the minimum.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS likely upgraded to 34–36p (+7–13% vs 31.8p) at June prelims. FY27 consensus held at 20.7p — the warehouse investment step-down (PBT guided £6.0m) is already fully reflected and management has explicitly confirmed in-line. TP likely raised modestly toward 430–450p from 415p; current price 245p reflects substantial structural discount given the FY27 drag, limiting the immediate re-rating. The key watch point: warehouse fit-out execution risk (£10.2m FY27 capex) — any cost overrun or disruption impacts FY27 PBT directly.

🏁 FY26 delivered a clean beat on all metrics; FY26 EPS upgrades of +7–13% highly probable; FY27 story constrained by known warehouse step-down — score 61/100.

Year label mappings: FY26 = FY1 (next year end 31/3/26) · FY25 = 1y ago · FY24 = 2y ago · FY23 = 3y ago · FY27 = FY2.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 11.3p · Revenue £36.4m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 23.0p · Revenue £38.8m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change −58.8% (27.4p → 11.3p) over full snapshot period. Downgrades heavily outnumbered upgrades. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT (no change since late Sept 25). Revenue net change: −3.4% (£37.7m → £36.4m).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 46.0% of FY = £16.7m · EPS 34.9% of FY = 3.9p (2yr avg)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £18.3m · EPS 13.8p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): Revenue: FY26fc £36.4m − H1 actual £17.1m = implied H2 £19.3m vs prior H2 £19.1m → +1.0% YoY. EPS: FY26fc 11.3p − H1 actual 0.9p = implied H2 10.4p vs prior H2 21.4p → −51.4% YoY.
  • FX: N/A — GBP reporting, no material non-GBP revenue identified.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net cash: FY23 −£0.3m → FY24 +£3.9m → FY25 +£4.1m → current H1 +£9.6m → FY26fc +£11.7m → FY27fc +£14.0m (all figures net cash, no debt). ND/EBITDA all negative (net cash). Interest cover: not applicable (net cash). Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

SYS1 · Q2 · Full Year Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Full Year Trading Update (Q4/Full Year)

  1. Revenue — FY26 actual: £37.0m, flat YoY vs FY25 £37.4m (−1.1%). Beat vs FY26fc consensus £36.4m by +£0.6m / +1.6%. H2 FY26 revenue: £19.8m vs H2 FY25 £19.1m = +3.7% YoY — record H2 performance. Platform Revenue £35.6m (+3% YoY) reversing H1 decline.

"Group revenue was steady at £37m (FY25: £37.4m) in line with previous guidance, demonstrating a strong recovery in Platform revenues in H2"

"H2 revenues increased 4% year on year, marking a record 6-month revenue performance"

  1. EPS / earnings — FY26 actual: Adjusted PBT £2.1m (consensus £2.0m, beat by +5%). Adjusted EBITDA £3.6m (FY25: £6.6m, −45%). The company states results are "slightly ahead of consensus." No EPS figure stated in this update — implied EPS derivation: PBT £2.1m, shares 12.7m; at ~25% tax → adj PAT ~£1.6m → adj EPS ~12.5p vs consensus 11.3p = +10.6% beat. Note: restructuring costs £0.5m separately disclosed.

"Adjusted PBT of £2.1m (FY25: £5.2m), in line with previous guidance"

"The Board is pleased to confirm trading in FY26 in line with guidance and slightly ahead of consensus"

FY27e EPS bridge (construct here):

  • New base: FY26 adj PBT £2.1m → implied adj EPS ~12.5p (estimated, pre formal accounts)
  • Inorganic annualisation delta: nil (no acquisitions)
  • Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY27fc EBITDA £5.7m vs FY26 actual £3.6m = +£2.1m uplift, driven by cost savings (£1m annualised) + revenue growth to £38.8m. Incremental EBIT uplift ~£1.9m after minor D&A step.
  • Interest step-up delta: nil — net cash, no debt drawdown
  • FY27e implied adj PBT: ~£4.2m (aligns with company-disclosed consensus); adj EPS ~£4.2m × 75% / 12.7m = ~24.8p. vs stale FY27fc consensus 23.0p = +7.8% revision implied.
  1. Order book / ARR equivalent: Over 300 new platform clients secured in FY26, delivering £10.7m revenue (30% of platform revenue). FY27 platform NRR was 72% in FY26 (FY25: 106%) — significant erosion, partially offset by new client wins. Active clients 626 vs 536 prior year (+17%). No order book figure disclosed. For ARR-model businesses: SYS1 has ≥80% recurring platform revenue — ARR coverage rule applies. ARR metric not explicitly disclosed in this update.

"Over 300 new platform clients were secured in the year, providing revenue of £10.7m, being 30% of full year Platform Revenue"

"FY26 Platform NRR of 72% (FY2025: 106%)"

  1. Margin/cost signals: EBITDA margin declined to ~9.7% (£3.6m/£37.0m) vs ~17.6% FY25. Cost savings of £1m annualised implemented H2. FY27 EBITDA margin guided "no less than 15%" (vs FY26 actual ~9.7%). This is a substantial guided recovery of ~5pp+. FY26 EBITDA contraction was wholly anticipated (investment year).

"Cost savings implemented in FY26 position the business for an improved EBITDA margin of no less than 15% in FY27, with the opportunity for further margin expansion as revenue scales"

  1. Capital returns: Cash £12.4m vs £12.9m prior year — near unchanged despite investment. DPS fc 3.7p FY26, 8.0p FY27.
  2. Qualitative tone: Board "comfortable with consensus Revenue forecasts for FY27 and the recently upgraded adjusted EBITDA expectations." Specifically mentions biggest ever sales contract signed in Q4 with new US client for delivery in FY27. Strong new business pipeline provides H2 FY27 revenue confidence.

"System1 concluded its biggest ever sales contract with a new US client in the final quarter which is expected to produce sales revenue in FY27"

EPS quality check: No tax distortion flagged; adj PBT figure used throughout. Restructuring costs £0.5m excluded from adjusted basis — appropriate.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward-looking statements cover FY27. Company explicitly "comfortable with consensus Revenue forecasts for FY27 and the recently upgraded adjusted EBITDA expectations." EBITDA margin guided "no less than 15%" — floor language on upgraded forecasts. Biggest-ever US contract for FY27 delivery is an explicit new earnings driver.

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — comfortable with upgraded EBITDA consensus, visible FY27 drivers (new US contract, cost savings), quantified margin floor. Points range: +6 to +10.

Guidance: qualitative + quantified margin floor · covers FY27 · language is confirmatory of recently upgraded numbers, not a new upgrade trigger.

No divergence: FY26 delivered in line/slightly ahead → FY27 guidance constructive. No contradiction.

  • EPS trend: net change −58.8% over snapshot period (27.4p → 11.3p). Two sharp step-downs: Jul 25 (upgrade to 38.3p) then Sep 25 (massive cut to 11.3p — investment programme announcement). No further moves since Sept 25.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Step 2: FY27fc EPS 23.0p > FY26 ~12.5p ✅✅. FY27fc Revenue £38.8m > FY26 £37.0m ✅✅.

3.6 Structural Flags

Investment year normalisation: FY26 EBITDA decline from £6.6m to £3.6m is entirely the result of the guided investment in sales and innovation capacity. The cost base has now been resized (£1m annualised savings implemented H2 FY26) and the platform now carries 626 active clients vs 536 prior year, providing a revenue base for FY27 growth.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

SYS1 · Q2 · Full Year Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

#1 Driver — FY27 EBITDA margin guidance and new US contract: The "no less than 15%" EBITDA margin floor for FY27, combined with the disclosure of SYS1's biggest-ever US sales contract for FY27 delivery, is the dominant catalyst. Brokers have been waiting seven months with frozen estimates (11.3p EPS) for confirmation that the investment year delivered as planned and FY27 growth is real. The margin floor guidance of 15%+ on £38.8m revenue = EBITDA ≥ £5.8m vs FY27fc £5.7m — a validation, not an upgrade, but it confirms the thesis.

#2 Driver — NRR erosion and platform retention risk: FY26 Platform NRR of 72% (vs 106% FY25) is a significant negative for a subscription-model business. While offset by new client wins, brokers will scrutinise whether existing customer churn is structural. This tempers enthusiasm for the upgrade cycle.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26 EPS: formal EPS not yet released; adj PBT £2.1m beats consensus £2.0m by ~5%. Revenue £37.0m beats £36.4m by +1.6%. Brokers likely to hold FY26 numbers pending July formal results — minor upward tilt possible (+2–5%).
  • FY27 EPS: margin guidance of ≥15% on revenue consensus £38.8m = EBITDA ≥ £5.82m vs fc £5.7m — hold / modest upgrade +0–5%. Revenue: company "comfortable with consensus" → hold. The bridge from EBITDA to EPS needs D&A (~£1.2m) and net interest credit (~£0.4m cash) → adj PBT ~£5.0m → EPS ~29.6p vs fc 23.0p. Wait — this implies a significant beat on the EPS bridge. Let me recheck: EBITDA £5.82m − D&A ~£1.2m = EBIT ~£4.6m + interest income ~£0.5m (net cash) = PBT ~£5.1m × 75% / 12.7m = ~30.1p vs fc 23.0p. That is a ~+31% implied upgrade from the margin floor alone. This is the key revision driver — brokers who rebuild the EPS bridge from the guided margin floor will upgrade FY27 EPS materially. Direction: upgrade, +15–30% range.
  • TP: consensus TP 446p — current price 291p, 53% upside already. Brokers likely to raise TPs, potentially back toward 400–500p range.

Conservative guidance read-through: "No less than 15%" is floor language — historically signals deliberate conservatism. "Comfortable with consensus" on revenue is also cautious phrasing. Combined, these suggest the actual FY27 EBITDA outcome could exceed the floor materially as revenue scales, implying upgrade cycle probability is elevated.

Key risk: NRR of 72% — if existing customer churn accelerates in FY27, new client additions may not fully offset, and the £38.8m revenue consensus could prove optimistic. Brokers will watch Q1 FY27 retention data closely.

"FY26 Platform NRR of 72% (FY2025: 106%)"

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely — margin floor guidance + new US contract confirm FY27 recovery thesis; formal accounts in July will trigger formal broker upgrades. Score deferred to Phase 5 given NRR headwind acting as a brake on full upgrade-cycle classification.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: SYS1 delivered FY26 revenue of £37.0m (consensus £36.4m, +1.6% beat) and adjusted PBT of £2.1m (consensus £2.0m, +5% beat), described as "slightly ahead of consensus." The standout catalyst is the H2 FY26 revenue of £19.8m — a record half-year and +3.7% YoY — confirming that the platform recovery flagged at H1 is real and accelerating into the year-end. EBITDA of £3.6m was in line with the pre-guided figure, reflecting the fully-anticipated investment year.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the implied H2 momentum is mixed — revenue H2 YoY +3.7% (🟡 moderate) but EPS H2 YoY −45.8% (🔴 severe), the latter wholly explained by the guided investment in sales headcount and restructuring charges totalling £0.5m. The bear case is capped: cost savings of £1m annualised are now embedded, cash is robust at £12.4m, and the guided EBITDA margin floor of ≥15% FY27 — applied to consensus revenue £38.8m — implies FY27 adj EBITDA ≥ £5.82m. Running the EPS bridge (EBITDA ≥ £5.82m − D&A ~£1.2m + interest income ~£0.5m = PBT ~£5.1m × 75% / 12.7m shares) yields implied FY27 EPS of ~30p, materially above the current stale consensus of 23.0p. The upgrade cycle is real but deferred to July full results.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are likely to formally upgrade FY27 EPS — the margin floor guidance alone supports a +15–30% revision to the 23.0p consensus. FY26 formal EPS will be confirmed in the July 8 results; expect minor upward revision (+2–5%) there. TP consensus is 446p vs current 291p — brokers are likely to reaffirm or raise toward 400–500p as the FY27 recovery thesis is now validated. The primary constraint on a higher score is the NRR erosion to 72% — if existing customer spend continues declining, new client additions may not fully offset, limiting the re-rating. Watch: Q1 FY27 trading update for evidence of NRR stabilisation.

🏁 FY26 delivered as guided; FY27 EBITDA margin floor ≥15% implies material EPS upgrades — formal upgrade cycle expected at July full results, constrained near-term by NRR risk and frozen consensus. Amber/constructive, score 54/100.

The order book doubling and "pipeline of new business remains strong" are the constructive signals embedded alongside the in-line confirmation. Key risk: The H2 delivery burden is extraordinary: £35.0m revenue in a single half-year (vs £24.4m H2 FY25 = highest prior H2). If Omantel implementation encounters delays — software integration complexity, customer-side readiness issues, milestone sign-off slippage — revenue recognition could shift into FY27, causing a FY26 miss. Para 1 — Headline numbers: The single defining signal in today's pre-H1 update is not the H1 numbers themselves — which are awful on the surface — but the order book doubling to £39.6m (H1 FY25: £19.6m), providing 113% contractual coverage of the £35.0m H2 revenue required to meet full-year consensus of £53.0m. H1 revenue of c.£18.0m (−14% vs H1 FY25 £20.9m) and H1 EBITDA of c.£6.2m (−37% vs H1 FY25 £9.9m) are the worst H1 figures in three years, but the company has pre-disclosed the reason explicitly: no high-margin software licence revenue was recognised in H1, entirely as anticipated. The Omantel contract (£42.5m, Cerillion's largest ever, signed January 2026) remains on track and is expected to "contribute significantly in the second half." The H1 miss is not a demand story — it is a revenue recognition timing event on a record contracted backlog.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H2 implied revenue of £35.0m (+43.4% vs H2 FY25 £24.4m) is the largest single-half revenue requirement in Cerillion's history — but it arrives with the most comprehensive contractual support the business has ever had. The order book of £39.6m excludes maintenance and support revenue, meaning total contracted H2 revenue (including recurring streams) comfortably covers the £35.0m target. Net cash of £32.5m — £5.0m better than Sharescope's H1 forecast — confirms the H1 miss is a P&L timing event only, not a cash or customer collection problem. The business is cash-generative and the Omantel milestone payments will reinforce this in H2. The one genuine risk is implementation delivery: if Omantel milestone sign-offs slip by even 4–6 weeks, meaningful licence revenue could fall into FY27, causing a FY26 miss despite the underlying demand being intact. Management's "on track" language is the key phrase — it confirms no slippage has emerged yet.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e EPS likely held at 58.4p and revenue at £53.0m — the in-line guidance gives brokers no basis to move. FY27e EPS (64.5p) carries upside risk that will be quantified at the 1 June interim results — the key catalyst for this name. If Omantel H2 progression is detailed at 1 June and further orders from existing customers are reported, FY27 upgrades toward 68–72p are plausible. The current consensus TP of £20.31 vs share price £14.30 represents 42% upside — an extreme gap for a business with net cash of £32.5m (worth ~110p/share alone), a doubled order book, and an in-line trading confirmation. The market is pricing a material H2 execution risk premium that today's update does not justify — "on track" is a clean confirmation. 🏁 In-line with record order book coverage and Omantel confirmed on track; the H1 miss is noise, the H2 setup is the most contractually supported in the company's history, and the real upgrade catalyst is 1 June.

#2 Driver — Medium-term targets (first-time disclosure): £120m rev / £15m EBITDA / 10% EBIT margin / 20% ROCE in 3–5 years vs FY27 consensus £90.5m / ~£8.8m EBITDA. Forecast revisions:

  • FY27e EPS: More significant revision — medium-term targets require modelling a Brazil growth path. Brokers likely revise FY27e EPS from 11.0p toward 12–14p range, revenue toward £95–105m. This is the bigger upgrade cycle.

Target price: Consensus TP 186p vs current 136.5p. Brokers likely to revise TPs upward to the 190–215p range on medium-term target announcement. Canaccord already at 190p — may move to 200–220p. The current share price discount (−27% vs TP) is unusually wide and provides significant re-rating potential.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with expectations" with company-compiled AOP consensus £5.5m is classic Fevara understatement given the H1 AOP of £7.2m already confirmed. Brokers will note that achieving the "in-line" AOP of £5.5m requires H2 AOP of −£1.7m — entirely consistent with seasonal patterns (H2 AOP FY25 was −£0.2m adjusted for central costs). The guidance is conservative, confirming downside is protected.

Key risk: Revenue was flat YoY at £50.6m — despite positive volume momentum (+6% LMB), the mix shift away from minerals and FX headwind suppressed reported revenue. If brokers focus on the revenue number rather than the margin-mix story, there is a risk of a muted reaction to the revenue line. Additionally, the H2 implied revenue burden of £35.0m (+24.1% YoY) — the highest H2 revenue required in the company's recent history — needs to be delivered, largely from Brazil. "Following the strategic entry in the significant Brazil market in December 2025, early trading has been in line with management's expectations."

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely for FY26e (upgrade quantum limited by H2 seasonality and management's in-line FY guidance); potentially 🟢🟢 upgrade cycle for FY27+ driven by medium-term targets. Para 1 — Headline numbers: The single defining number from today's H1 results is adj EPS of 11.0p (+116% vs H1 FY25 5.1p), which has already exceeded the entire FY26 consensus EPS of 8.3p by 32.5% with six months of the financial year still to run. The H1 adj operating profit of £7.2m (+22% YoY) on essentially flat revenue of £50.6m (flat reported, +2% constant currency) reveals a business undergoing genuine margin transformation: H1 EBIT margin of 14.2% vs 11.7% prior year, with central costs slashed 27% YoY to £0.8m. The EPS step-change is partly structural (share count halved post-tender offer) but the underlying PBT growth of +18.6% and 250bp margin expansion confirm that the operational transformation is real and tracking ahead of broker models. LTM adj operating profit is now £5.0m (+35% from FY25 £3.7m), which management is rightly flagging as the relevant forward indicator.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The revenue tracking signal is problematic on a mechanical basis: H1 revenue at £50.6m represents only 59.1% of the £85.6m FY1 consensus, versus a 2-year seasonal average of 63.3% — a −4.2pp deviation that triggers a SELL SIGNAL on the revenue metric alone. This is misleading as a signal: the shortfall is entirely explained by a deliberate planned reduction in lower-margin mineral volumes (UK/Ireland minerals −14% by design) and the FX translation headwind on US revenues (~45% of the business, GBP ~5c stronger vs prior year). LMB volumes — the core premium product — were actually +6% YoY (UK/Europe +9%, US owned +4%). The H2 implied revenue burden of £35.0m vs £28.2m prior (+24.1%) requires delivery on Macal (full H2 contribution), gradual São Paulo ramp, and continuation of the southern US momentum (+28% volume H1). Management explicitly states "trading since the half year has been encouraging...US overall trading is ahead of the prior year." The H2 weather normalisation in the northern US (second warmest winter in 132 years in H1 is not an H2 problem) provides a natural tailwind. The upgrade resilience case is therefore strong: even in a bear scenario where Brazil contributes minimally to H2, the organic business is generating sufficient margin to protect FY26 adj EPS well above the stale 8.3p consensus.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers must revise FY26e adj EPS from 8.3p — the question is the landing point. Edison (8.6p FY26e) and Canaccord (8.5p) are both stale; with H1 at 11.0p and H2 guided as seasonally loss-making (consistent with H2 FY25 −0.7p adj EPS), FY26e likely lands at 8.5–9.5p (our central estimate ~9.0p, implying H2 adj EPS of approximately −1.5 to −2.0p). FY27e revision is larger — medium-term targets require modelling a Brazil growth path and central cost normalisation that pushes consensus from 11.0p toward 12–14p range. Revenue consensus may hold near £85.6m for FY26 given the flat H1 print, with FY27 moving toward £95–100m+ as Brazil contribution is modelled. Consensus TP at 186p vs current 136.5p = 36.5% upside — this gap has become extreme given the EPS delivery, and a re-rating toward 160–175p on today's results would be a modest response; the medium-term target announcement justifies revisiting broker DCFs with significantly higher terminal earnings assumptions. The dominant watch point is broker treatment of the revenue line — if any house flags the flat H1 revenue as a negative without properly contextualising the margin mix story, the re-rating will be slower. 🏁 Compelling H1 delivery on the metrics that matter — adj EPS dramatically ahead of consensus, margins expanding sharply, medium-term targets set for the first time — with the revenue flatness entirely explained by a value-accretive mix shift; the score is constrained by the FX drag and the mechanical revenue tracking signal but the fundamental upgrade cycle is confirmed.

On a reported basis, adj OP grew £0.5m on £2.3m revenue increase = ~22% drop-through — low but explained by FX and mix.
  • FY26 adj EPS: not disclosed in this trading update. Full results 2 June 2026. Sharescope consensus 18.7p — likely to be validated at full results. Buyback (~8% equity reduction in FY26) is a structural EPS tailwind — 232.5m shares outstanding vs likely ~213–215m post-buyback. This means reported EPS may modestly beat consensus on a per-share basis even if PBT is in-line.
  • Implied FY26 EPS bridge: Adj OP ~£67.5m + interest income net (moderate; net debt £80m at ~5% → net interest charge ~£2-3m) → adj PBT ~£65m. Tax at 25% → PAT ~£49m. On ~215m shares post-buyback → EPS ~22.7p. Wait — Sharescope consensus is 18.7p on 232.5m shares. If shares have been reduced by ~8% buyback, the weighted average for FY26 may be ~220m → EPS = £49m / 220m = ~22.3p. This materially exceeds 18.7p consensus. ⚠️ Either: (a) my adj PBT estimate is too high (likely — adj OP includes D&A/lease adjustments); or (b) Sharescope share count of 232.5m is the pre-buyback count and EPS consensus was calculated on the pre-buyback count. In practice, GBG's adj EPS is calculated differently (includes amortisation/interest in different configurations). Without the full results, the EPS figure cannot be precisely derived. Flag: per-share items from buyback (8% of equity = ~18.6m shares at a cost of £45m average ~242p) will provide EPS uplift vs a model that used beginning-of-year share count. This is a known positive.

  • Implied FY26e adj EPS: ~17.4 + 0.2 + 1.1 − 0.2 = ~18.5p — closely aligned with consensus 18.7p. Bridge confirms consensus is accurate. No material revision expected from today's trading update.

3. Order book / pipeline:

  • GBG Go platform: "90 wins... more than a quarter with multi-solution requirement." Pipeline: "225+ opportunities entering FY27."
  • Americas Identity "returned to growth in Q4." EMEA "strong execution." These are qualitative positive signals for FY27.

This is quantitative guidance: FY27 rev growth mid-single-digits = ~5–6% from £285m base = £298–302m — broadly consistent with consensus £298.9m. No EPS guidance for FY27.

B. OUTLOOK & GUIDANCE CLASSIFICATION

FY27 guidance: "mid-single-digit revenue growth" — numeric, quantitative range (5–6%), covering FY27 only. This matches consensus £298.9m closely. No EPS guidance. The GBG Go platform pipeline of 225+ opportunities and the Americas return to growth in Q4 provide qualitative support.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — FY27 revenue guidance matches consensus (mid-single-digit = ~5%); adj OP margin held flat for FY26; no explicit EPS upgrade trigger. The H2 core segment acceleration (+6% CC) is a constructive data point that may support minor FY27 upgrades. Provisional points: +2.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: GBG confirmed a clean FY26 in-line delivery: £285m revenue (+3.2% CC, +0.8% reported) and adj operating profit ~£67.5m (margin 23.7%, flat vs FY25's 23.7%), both matching Sharescope consensus of £284.9m / 18.7p EPS. The single most positive element of this announcement is not the headline in-line delivery — it is the core Identity and Location segment growth accelerating to +6% CC in H2, compared to a weak H1. Americas Identity, which had been a drag on the business, returned to growth in Q4 — a genuine inflection point after a period of investor concern. The FY26 adj EPS is not disclosed in this trading update (full results 2 June 2026), but the bridge from FY25 17.4p through adj OP performance and ~8% buyback accretion points to consensus 18.7p as an accurate estimate.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The implied H2 FY26 revenue of £149.5m (+2.5% YoY vs H2 FY25 £145.8m) — classified as 🟡 moderate — understates the quality of the H2 delivery because the legacy Compliance platform decline is embedded in the group revenue figure. The core segment growth at +6% CC in H2 is a materially better signal. GBG Go's 225+ FY27 pipeline opportunities and the expansion of cross-sell (>25% of wins multi-solution) provide a credible FY27 upgrade path that is not yet in the flat consensus EPS trajectory. The downgrade concern — adj OP margin held flat at 23.7% — is real: for a business investing in a new platform (GBG Go), maintaining margin while growing is acceptable, but it does not provide the operating leverage signal that would accelerate the upgrade cycle. Net debt of £80m is higher than the Sharescope forecast of £63.1m, explained entirely by the £45m buyback at an average price that looks well below the 360p TP consensus, providing ongoing EPS accretion from the new £10m buyback commenced 1 April.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: At full results on 2 June 2026, the key variables are: (1) FY26 adj EPS (consensus 18.7p; buyback accretion may produce a modest beat); (2) FY27 guidance specificity — "mid-single-digit revenue growth" matches consensus £298.9m, but any EPS guidance would be the upgrade trigger; (3) Americas and GBG Go pipeline commentary. FY26e EPS likely held at 18.7p; FY27e EPS may see modest upgrades toward 20–21p on Americas recovery modelling, from current 20.8p (consensus already has some of this). Consensus TP 360p vs current 213p = 69% upside — this is an extreme discount for a FTSE 250 identity tech business delivering in-line, but reflects the market's concern about reported revenue growth trajectory and GBP headwinds. The 2 June full results are the real catalyst. 🏁 In-line delivery with a positive H2 acceleration narrative — the H2 +6% CC core growth and Americas inflection are genuine positives that should support the current consensus, but the flat margin and sluggish reported revenue trajectory mean today's announcement is unlikely to drive material re-rating; the real test is the 2 June full results and FY27 guidance.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

LBG · Q4 · Half-Year Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update / Half-Year Trading Update (H1 ended 31 March 2026)

1. Revenue — H1 FY26:

  • H1 revenue: £52.4m (+19% YoY vs H1 FY25 £43.9m; +22% constant currency).

"Strong revenue momentum, up 19% to £52.4m (H1 25: £43.9m). Constant currency revenue growth of 22%."

2. Adj EBITDA / EPS — H1 FY26:

  • H1 adj EBITDA: £8.0m (H1 FY25: £12.2m) = −34.4% YoY.
  • vs FY26 consensus £25.4m full year: H1 = £8.0m = 31.5% of FY consensus vs H1 FY25 = £12.2m / £25.4m FY consensus = 48.0% of FY consensus. Massive underperformance vs seasonal baseline on EBITDA.
  • FY26 adj EBITDA guided to c.£22m vs consensus £25.4m = cut of −£3.4m = −13.4% on EBITDA. This is the profit warning component.
  • EPS (adj): not disclosed. With EBITDA cut from £25.4m to £22m, EPS revision: adj EBITDA − (D&A ~£2m + net interest income ~£0.5m) → adj PBT ~£20.5m at FY22 guidance → tax ~25% → PAT ~£15.4m → EPS on 209.1m shares = ~7.3p. vs consensus 7.5p = cut of ~−3%. More severe depending on D&A structure. EPS revision likely −5 to −10% from 7.5p to ~6.8–7.1p.

"Lower adjusted EBITDA of £8.0m (H1 25 £12.2m), reflecting three key factors."

EPS bridge FY26e (updated):

  • (1) New base: FY25 adj EPS 6.7p (full year). H1 FY26 adj EPS not disclosed; EBITDA £8.0m H1 vs £22m FY guidance → H2 implied EBITDA = £14.0m.
  • (2) EBITDA cut: FY guidance £22m vs consensus £25.4m → −£3.4m → EPS cut ~−0.7p on 209m shares after tax → revised FY26e EPS ~6.8–7.1p.
  • (3) Revenue upgrade: £110m vs £105m → +£5m revenue but at lower EBITDA margin → incremental revenue is from Direct (lower margin than Indirect).
  • Implied FY26e EPS: ~6.8–7.1p (centred ~7.0p) vs stale consensus 7.5p = cut of ~−6 to −9%.

3. EBITDA margin drivers — three stated factors:

  1. Planned investment in senior leadership and US/UK Direct sales capability.
  2. Revenue and margin mix moving toward Direct revenue (>70% in H1; FY25 ~55%) — Direct has lower margins than Indirect.
  3. No recovery in Indirect revenue (algorithmic/platform revenue-sharing) — Meta Facebook algorithm changes continuing; "referral volumes...in line with trends experienced in H2 25."

"Lower adjusted EBITDA...reflecting three key factors. Firstly, planned investment in senior leadership and sales capability...Secondly, revenue and margin mix moving towards Direct revenue streams...Thirdly, we did not see a recovery in our Indirect revenue streams."

4. Qualitative — H2 outlook and EBITDA recovery:

  • "H2 26 weighting for adjusted EBITDA reflects the benefit of senior hires, as well as cost savings made in H1 26." Implied H2 EBITDA: £22m − £8.0m = £14.0m vs H1 £8.0m — £6m H2 loading. H2 FY25 adj EBITDA = £12.2m (full year £25.4m consensus H1 portion £12.2m of £25.4m = 48% in H1 → H2 FY25 ~£13.2m). H2 FY26 guided £14.0m vs H2 FY25 ~£13.2m = +6.1% YoY. Plausible but reliant on senior hire benefits crystallising and cost savings in H1 carrying forward.
  • "Excellent momentum from Direct revenue streams...healthy pipeline for H2."
  • Meta/Facebook indirect headwind "continuing in line with trends experienced in H2 25" — no recovery expected.

5. Cash position:

  • Net cash £28.4m (31 Mar 2026) vs FY25 £30.8m. Slight decline driven by investment.
  • "Strong balance sheet and cash generation continues to support selective acquisitions."

6. Guidance Summary (Post-RNS):

  • FY26 Revenue: upgraded to c.£110m (from £105m consensus) = +4.8% upgrade.
  • FY26 adj EBITDA: guided to c.£22m (from £25.4m consensus) = −13.4% cut.
  • This is a revenue upgrade / EBITDA warning combination — the quality of earnings has deteriorated (Direct revenue at lower margins, Indirect structural decline continuing).

B. OUTLOOK & GUIDANCE CLASSIFICATION

The RNS contains simultaneous revenue upgrade (+4.8%) and EBITDA profit warning (−13.4%). This is a textbook Beat quality divergence.

FY26 guidance: numeric, explicit: revenue £110m (above consensus) but EBITDA £22m (below consensus). The RNS is honest about the causes: margin mix (Direct lower-margin than Indirect), investment, and Indirect structural decline.

Classification: 🔴 Cautious — EBITDA below consensus, margin dilution from structural Indirect decline, investment spend flagged. Despite revenue upgrade, the earnings quality is deteriorating. Provisional points: −6 to −8 pts.

Divergence check: Revenue beat vs EBITDA miss = explicit divergence. Current H1 revenue strongly growing (+19% YoY) but EBITDA sharply declining (−34%). Flag: 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery — revenue growth momentum positive but earnings quality declining. This is a separate scored row.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Now I have both documents. Working from the actual disclosures chronologically.

When was the Indirect decline first visible in the numbers?

H1 FY25 results (June 2025) — the numbers looked fine on the surface

H1 FY25 reported Indirect revenue up 18% to £24.5m. Adjusted EBITDA up 18% to £12.2m. Margin improved to 27.8% from 26.4%. On the face of it, no alarm. But there was a tell buried in the segmental detail: the 18% Indirect growth was explicitly described as being against "a weak prior year comparator on social platforms" and Social specifically grew 12% — which management attributed to "improved platform performance versus a softer prior year." That "softer prior year" was itself caused by Facebook algorithm changes, meaning the H1 FY25 Social growth was bounce, not acceleration.

Web grew 27% in H1 FY25 — a genuinely strong number but attributed to resolution of "prior period web-related issues," again signalling the comparison base was distorted.

So the first numerical warning sign was not the headline EBITDA margin — it was the quality of the Indirect growth. H1 FY25 Indirect growth was entirely base-effect driven. Strip that out and the underlying trajectory of the Social revenue stream was flat to slightly declining in absolute terms relative to a normalised prior period.

The content costs line was the other signal that gets ignored: up 29% in H1 FY25 while revenue grew only 13%. Content costs growing at 2.2x the rate of revenue is a margin compression indicator even when EBITDA margin looks healthy, because it means the business is working harder per pound of revenue. The H1 FY25 EBITDA margin of 27.8% was flattered by Indirect performing on a weak comp and held up because overhead growth was disciplined. Remove the comp benefit and the underlying margin was already under pressure.

The current trading section of H1 FY25 (June 2025) was the most direct signal available. Management stated: "Within our Indirect business, we have seen the impact of macro and tariff uncertainty on advertising spend and advertising yields since the half year." And specifically: "We are seeing a steady build-up in our Social revenue stream and a stabilisation in the Web revenue stream." "Stabilisation" in Web after the prior year's Web decline is not a recovery — it means flat. And the language on Social ("steady build-up") is deliberately modest, contrasting with the 12% and 18% growth figures they were reporting for H1.

That current trading paragraph, combined with the FX headwind warning (£2m revenue, £1m EBITDA impact), was the signal. Anyone reading it carefully in June 2025 at ~110p had the information to ask: if Indirect is merely "stabilising" post-H1 and Direct is the only growth engine, what does the margin mix look like in H2 and into FY26?

FY25 full year results (February 2026) — the deterioration became explicit

By the time the FY25 results landed the picture was fully disclosed:

Indirect Web declined −13% on a like-for-like 12-month basis (£16.2m vs £18.7m). Management attributed this to "weaker referral volumes and a tough prior-year comparator." The prior-year comparator for Web was itself inflated by the resolution of prior-period web issues in H1 FY25 — so the Web revenue line was distorting the picture in both directions across consecutive periods.

Indirect Social grew 12% for the full year — but the year-end exit rate matters more than the annual average. The current trading section of the FY25 results states for H1 FY26 outlook: "We expect our higher growth Direct revenue streams to make up an increasing proportion of Group revenue (expected to exceed 50% of Group revenues and potentially reaching 70%)." Indirect was already at 45% of FY25 revenues, down from 56% in H1 FY25. That trajectory — 56% → 45% → expected <30% — is a structural decline in the highest-margin revenue stream embedded in the guidance.

The FY25 results also introduced for the first time explicit margin guidance by segment: Direct margins "before central costs in the mid-20% range" vs Indirect margins "remaining above 50%." This was the disclosure that made the EBITDA margin compression mechanically calculable. If Direct grows from 54% to 70% of revenues at 20-something percent margin, while Indirect (50%+ margin) shrinks proportionally, the blended group EBITDA margin must fall — and the company acknowledged this by saying Group EBITDA margins would "remain in line with consensus." That consensus at the time was £25.4m adj EBITDA on £105m revenue = 24.2% margin, down from 27.4% in FY25. The guidance was essentially flagging a 300bp+ margin compression was already baked in.

What would the first numerical signal have been for a quantitative investor?

Not EBITDA margin at the headline level — that was still expanding in H1 FY25. The first quantitative signal was:

Content costs as a % of revenue growing faster than revenue — H1 FY25: content costs 17.3% of revenue vs H1 FY24: 15.2%. That's a 210bp increase in the content cost ratio. For a business where Indirect revenue required near-zero incremental content cost (platforms pay you based on existing content), rising content cost ratio indicates the mix is shifting toward Direct (which requires actively commissioned content) faster than the revenue split suggests.

The second was the note about Social revenue in H1 FY25 being against a "weak prior year comparator." When a company describes its own growth number with reference to a weak comp rather than absolute demand, that is an implicit acknowledgement that the absolute level of Social revenue in H1 FY24 was abnormally low, and the H1 FY25 growth does not represent a sustainable run-rate.

On the share price timing — 110p in June 2025 to 48p now

The H1 FY25 results at 110p in June 2025 contained the current trading warning on Indirect and the FX headwind disclosure. The H2 FY25 would have been the period (April–September 2025) where Indirect Web was declining 13% and Social was stabilising rather than growing. The FY25 full results in February 2026 then confirmed the strategic pivot — essentially management saying the business is deliberately shrinking its highest-margin revenue stream while investing heavily to replace it with lower-margin Direct. The market had been pricing that transition risk progressively since June 2025.

Today's H1 FY26 update shows the transition is happening faster than consensus assumed: Indirect EBITDA contribution is collapsing (H1 EBITDA £8m vs £12.2m prior, −34%) while the revenue replacement from Direct (+19% top line) hasn't come with sufficient margin to compensate. The £22m FY26 EBITDA guidance vs £25.4m consensus is the finalisation of a process that was visible in outline from June 2025 if you looked at content cost ratios, the quality of the Indirect growth figures, and the current trading language carefully.
