PINE · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results (12 months ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY25 actual:

  • Revenue: £40.5m (FY24: £31.2m) = +29.8% YoY on a reported basis. However FY24 was 11 months vs FY25 12 months — on a comparable annualised basis FY24 revenue = £31.2m × (12/11) = £34.0m annualised → FY25 +19.1% on annualised comparable.
  • vs Sharescope FY1 fc £41.7m: miss of −£1.2m = −2.9%.
  • Recurring revenue: £33.7m = 83.2% of total (FY24: 86.5%). Slight decline in recurring mix — Seez AI bringing some non-recurring implementation revenue.
  • H1: £19.6m / H2: £20.9m — modest H2 weighting, consistent with 2yr avg split.

"Revenue up 29.8% to £40.5m in FY25 (from £31.2m in FY24)...the revenue growth was due to a combination of FY24 being an 11 month period and FY25 being a 12 month period, the Seez acquisition in March 2025, revenue from new customers and revenue from upselling."

2. EPS / Earnings — FY25:

  • Underlying PAT: £5.7m (FY24: £6.4m) = −10.9% YoY. On 104.7m shares = 5.4p underlying adj EPS.
  • vs FY1 fc 6.0p consensus: miss of −0.6p = −10%.
  • Underlying EBITDA: £16.4m vs fc £15.8m = +3.8% beat.
  • Underlying PBT: £8.8m vs fc £8.8m = in-line exactly.
  • The EBITDA beat / EPS miss paradox: EBITDA £16.4m beat, but underlying PAT fell from FY24 £6.4m to FY25 £5.7m. The bridge: EBITDA £16.4m → D&A £8.1m (up £2.5m YoY, driven by Seez intangibles amortisation) → underlying EBIT £8.3m → net finance income £0.5m → underlying PBT £8.8m → tax £3.1m (effective rate 35.2% vs FY24 rate 24.8%) → underlying PAT £5.7m. The EPS miss vs EBITDA beat is entirely explained by (a) D&A step-up from Seez acquisition (£7.0m amortisation in FY25 vs £5.0m FY24) and (b) the higher effective tax rate (35.2% vs 24.8% prior year). Both reduce EPS below what the EBITDA beat implies.

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate 35.2% vs prior 24.8% = +10.4pp. This is a significant deviation. If restated at 24.8% normalised rate: underlying PAT = £8.8m × (1 − 0.248) = £6.62m → EPS = 6.3p — which would have beaten consensus 6.0p. The tax rate increase is the primary driver of the EPS miss. The RNS does not explain the higher effective tax rate. The deferred tax liability jumped from £2.5m to £35.0m — a £32.5m increase driven by the Seez AI acquisition intangibles recognition for tax purposes. This is acquisition accounting-driven, not indicative of underlying trading deterioration. 🚨 Flag: EPS miss is tax-driven (acquisition accounting), not operational. Restated normalised EPS ~6.3p would have been a beat.

EPS bridge FY26e (constructed here):

  • (1) New base: FY25 underlying EPS 5.4p (at 35.2% effective tax rate) or 6.3p (at normalised 24.8%). Using 5.4p as reported base.
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: Seez acquired March 2025 → contributed ~10 months in FY25. Full 12-month Seez contribution in FY26 = ~2 additional months → incremental EBITDA ~£0.7m. Also Netherlands reseller acquired Feb 2026 → £0.7–0.8m EBITDA additive in FY26.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: Company guides FY26 underlying EBITDA consensus = £21.3m (confirmed in RNS footnote). FY25 = £16.4m → FY26 = £21.3m = +£4.9m = +29.9% YoY growth. Revenue consensus FY26 = £57.8m vs FY25 £40.5m = +42.7% — very large step-up implying Lookers rollout completion and Lithia early revenue recognition.
  • (4) Interest step-up: Net cash £34.1m → growing; interest income growing. No step-up concern.

Key risk: Execution slippage on large enterprise rollouts. The Marshalls delay has established a pattern. Lookers is "progressing well" but due to finish Q4 2026 — a tight window. Lithia US is at "system testing" stage, which is pre-revenue. The FY28 EBITDA target requires multiple large contracts all executing on schedule simultaneously. "The implementation of the Pinewood.AI platform across Lookers' dealerships is progressing well and is due to finish in Q4 2026."

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline tension in Pinewood's FY25 results is the gap between the metrics that matter to the underlying business and the reported EPS outcome. On the metrics that matter: underlying EBITDA of £16.4m beat consensus £15.8m by +3.8%; TCV reached £64.5m in signed contracted future revenue; North America OEM integration is at ~90% completion; and the FY28 EBITDA target of £58–62m has been explicitly reaffirmed with 85% of the projected growth already under signed contract. On the reported headline: underlying EPS of 5.4p missed consensus 6.0p by 10% — entirely explained by a deferred tax liability step-up from Seez AI acquisition accounting (£32.5m DTL increase) pushing the effective tax rate from 24.8% to 35.2%. At a normalised 24.8% tax rate, EPS would have been ~6.3p — a beat. Revenue of £40.5m missed £41.7m consensus by 2.9%, a modest shortfall driven by the annualisation period difference vs FY24 and Seez revenue mix. The operational delivery is sound; the noise is acquisition accounting.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY25 revenue of £20.9m (+38.4% vs H2 FY24 £15.1m) and H2 EBITDA of £8.5m (+21.4% YoY) confirm the second-half weighting of the growth trajectory is intact. The 🟢 strong H2 classification is RNS-derived and contractually supported. The critical forward risk is the Marshalls delay: previously expected Q1 2026, now H2 2026. This six-month slip will compress H1 FY26 revenue and EBITDA vs the 48.3% seasonal baseline, almost certainly generating a SELL SIGNAL on the H1 tracking metric in the next update — but it is a timing event, not a cancellation. Lookers (completion Q4 2026) and Lithia US (system testing underway) are the two other execution dependencies. The upgrade resilience case rests entirely on these three programmes delivering on revised schedules. The FY26 EBITDA consensus of £21.3m (company-confirmed) implies £4.9m EBITDA growth YoY — achievable from Lookers and Seez full-year contribution even without Marshalls in H1, but with zero margin for further slippage. Net cash of £34.1m provides runway, though the FY26 FCF forecast of only £1.8m highlights that the investment phase is consuming cash aggressively.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY25 EPS brokers revise from 6.0p to approximately 5.4p (−10%); the EBITDA beat provides some offset and TP reductions are unlikely given the FY28 reaffirmation. FY26 EPS from 9.3p current consensus — at risk of modest cuts toward 8.0–8.5p driven by the Marshalls H1 timing slip and continuing North America pre-revenue losses, partially offset by Seez full-year contribution. FY26 revenue consensus £57.8m may be trimmed toward £54–56m if Marshalls H2 ramp takes time to crystallise. Consensus TP 654p vs current 232p = 181% implied upside — the gap reflects the market pricing a significant execution risk premium onto the FY28 DCF. This is a binary story: if Lookers completes Q4 2026 on schedule, Lithia US moves from testing to rollout, and Marshalls starts H2 as guided, the FY28 target remains credible and the 232p price is deeply cheap. If any further slippage emerges, the FY28 timeline extends and the multiple contracts further. 🏁 FY25 delivered on the metrics that matter — EBITDA ahead, TCV at record, FY28 reaffirmed with 85% contracted — but the execution credibility deficit from the Marshalls delay, the EPS miss (accounting-driven), and the near-zero FY26 FCF forecast leave the score squarely in neutral territory; the real catalyst is H1 FY26 delivery and any Lookers/Lithia update.

Three things worth flagging on PINE specifically:

The −31% EPS downgrade cycle before results is significant context — the market already knew FY25 would disappoint vs original 8.9p expectations, so today's 5.4p print is not a shock. But it also means there's little to upgrade from here on FY25; the debate shifts entirely to FY26 and FY28.

The EPS miss being tax-driven is genuinely important and something a broker note will need to address explicitly — because it means the underlying business generated £8.8m PBT in-line with consensus, and the 5.4p vs 6.0p gap is purely the deferred tax liability from Seez intangibles winding through the P&L. A normalised EPS of ~6.3p would have been a beat. Brokers who model normalised tax rates will frame FY25 as an operational beat, not a miss.

The 232p price vs 654p Sharescope TP is flagged in the sparkline — the price collapse from ~650p to 232p since the Marshalls delay (25 Mar) is embedded in the chart and visible. That's where the real story is today: not the results themselves, but whether management's FY28 reaffirmation is enough to arrest a share that has lost two-thirds of its value in under a month.

Q1 ARR grew £1.6m in the period to £38.6m on a constant-currency basis, representing 12% TTM growth and providing 95.8% coverage of the full-year revenue consensus — an extraordinary forward visibility figure for any business. The standout positive data point is net revenue retention improving from 95.7% to 98.1% over the twelve months to 31 March 2026, indicating that the installed base is churning less and expanding more. The headline negative is also explicitly flagged: new subscriptions were −13% in Q1 and new customers −8%, compared against what management characterise as a "particularly strong" Q1 2025. Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e EPS and revenue consensus likely to be held at 16.2p / £40.3m — the in-line statement gives brokers no justification to move. FY27e EPS at 16.4p (barely +1.2% growth) may attract modest upward revision from NRR improvement modelling, but the new subscription deceleration will temper enthusiasm. Consensus TP 360p vs current 277.5p = 29.7% upside — the TP discount is wide and reflects the market's scepticism about the pace of the new business recovery. The main watch-point is whether Q1 new subscription weakness normalises in Q2 (i.e., base effect) or whether it persists into a structural deceleration thesis. The France 4G upgrade completing in FY26 is a near-term positive that reduces churn risk and could support NRR improvement into FY27. 🏁 An in-line, high-visibility business that has already been re-rated to reflect improved profitability, but with the new subscription deceleration as the key risk that prevents a further upgrade from today's update.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Data source gate: This is a Q2 trading update providing AUA and customer data only — no H1 revenue or EPS figures disclosed. RNS conditions (1), (2), (3) all unmet. Both metrics: UNTRACKABLE.

Note: AUA £110.2bn at 31 March 2026 (+20% YoY) is a strong leading indicator. If management fee yield is ~0.24% on AUA, implied annualised revenue = £264m platform fees. Total revenue £348.7m consensus includes other items. AUA trajectory is very positive for revenue tracking.

Revenue baseline for FY26 H1: 3yr avg H1% = 47.4%. £348.7m × 47.4% = £165.3m. Buy trigger: £165.3m × 1.015 = £167.8m. H1 results (21 May 2026) will be the tracking date.

EPS baseline for FY26 H1: 3yr avg H1% = 48.3%. 26.1p × 48.3% = 12.6p. Buy trigger: 12.6p × 1.015 = 12.8p.

Signal: UNTRACKABLE (no H1 revenue or EPS in RNS). H1 results expected 21 May 2026.

Implied H1 from AUA leading indicator: AUA growth +20% YoY is a proxy for revenue growth. If revenue grows at a similar rate: FY25 H1 £131.3m × 1.20 = £157.6m implied H1 revenue. vs baseline £165.3m: deviation = £157.6m/£348.7m = 45.2% vs 47.4% baseline → indicative deviation −2.2pp. Flag as 🟡 PROBABLE CAUTION (implied deviation ≤ −1.5pp — AUA growth rate does not fully translate to revenue growth at same rate due to mix shift in fees). However: the D2C gross inflows were +42% YoY in Q2 — D2C customers carry higher margin. This partially offsets the AUA lag.

Flag explicitly: "H1 unconfirmed — signal derived from AUA leading indicator only. Revenue/AUA yield assumption critical. Confirm on H1 results 21 May 2026."

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-H1 mode)

Implied H2 Revenue: £183.4m vs 3yr avg (FY23 H2 £88.3m, FY24 H2 £114.6m, FY25 H2 £164.6m) avg = £122.5m. Implied H2 £183.4m vs avg £122.5m → +49.7% above 3yr avg. 🟢 strong — but this primarily reflects platform growth scale effect (FY25 H2 alone was £164.6m; consensus H2 FY26 is £183.4m = +11.4% YoY — manageable).

Implied H2 EPS: 13.5p vs 3yr avg (FY23 H2 6.3p, FY24 H2 8.5p, FY25 H2 13.4p) avg = 9.4p. Implied H2 EPS 13.5p vs avg 9.4p → +43.6% above 3yr avg. YoY: 13.5p vs FY25 H2 13.4p → essentially flat. Classification: 🟡 flat (YoY basis) / 🟢 strong (vs 3yr avg — but base effect from FY25 exceptional year).

The real concern is that H2 EPS is essentially flat at 13.5p vs 13.4p FY25 H2 despite +20% AUA growth and +22% customer growth. This suggests significant investment spending in H2 or fee compression from competitive pricing.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

Reporting currency: GBP.

Net cash throughout. FY26e fc net cash £196.2m — growing. No leverage risk. ND/EBITDA all negative. Interest cover: negative (cash generates income).

3.6 Structural flags

[Interest rate sensitivity]: AJB's H2 FY25 revenue surge (+44%) was partly driven by higher interest rates on client cash balances. Rate cuts (BoE cutting in 2025) compress the cash income element. This is why FY26e EPS consensus is +1.2% despite AUA +20% — the interest rate tailwind is fading.

[D2C momentum step-change]: D2C customers +28% YoY to 534,000 from 416,000. D2C is higher-margin and growing faster than Advised. Mix shift towards D2C is structurally positive for unit economics. Q2 FY26 saw record D2C customer growth (+46k net in single quarter, >50% above prior year same quarter).

[Investment step-up flag]: CEO language: "early benefits of our previously announced increased investment in our brand and propositions." PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

FOXT · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Q1 2026 Trading Update, 3 months ended 31 March 2026)

1. Revenue figures

Q1 2026 Group revenue: £39.6m (Q1 2025: £44.1m), −10% YoY.

By segment: Lettings £26.4m (+5%); Sales £10.7m (−35%); Financial Services £2.6m (+3%).

No full-year numeric guidance stated. The RNS states "full year guidance remains unchanged." This is qualitative only — no quantification of the unchanged guidance figure.

Q1 2025 had an exceptionally strong comparator from elevated stamp duty deadline volumes. Vs Q1 2024 (normalised): like-for-like Sales revenue +£0.2m above Q1 2024's £9.5m — LFL basis effectively flat.

"The Group is trading in line with previous expectations and full year guidance remains unchanged."

"Sales revenue declined by 35% to £10.7m (Q1 2025: £16.4m), reflecting an exceptionally strong prior-year comparator that benefited from elevated transaction volumes ahead of the 31 March 2025 stamp duty deadline."

2. EPS / earnings figures

No Q1 EPS disclosed (trading update only). No H1 EPS figures. Annual EPS guidance not provided. FY guidance "unchanged" but no numeric EPS guide restated.

FY26e EPS bridge (construct here):

  • (1) New base EPS actual (FY25): Sharescope shows FY25 EPS as current H1 2.7p + H2 2.2p = 4.9p (or FY actual). FY1 fc 5.0p implies a +0.1p step-up from 4.9p actual — a very modest upgrade in consensus already baked in.
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: Two acquisitions completed in Q1 2026 (Milton Keynes and Birmingham lettings businesses). No revenue quantum disclosed for these acquisitions individually. However, RNS states Q1 Lettings acquisition contribution = £0.9m of the £1.2m Lettings YoY increase. Annualising Q1 £0.9m acquisition contribution × 4 quarters ≈ £3.6m incremental annualised revenue. At Foxtons' Lettings operating margin (~18% EBIT margin on Lettings), this is approximately £0.65m incremental EBIT or ~0.2p EPS annualisation uplift for FY26.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: Q1 organic Lettings growth = £0.6m. Organic Lettings trajectory modest positive (+2.3% organic). Sales market subdued — £10.7m vs £9.5m LFL (Q1 2024 normalised basis), so flat to marginally positive on normalised basis. Cost reduction programme (£3m+ annualised) and £1.5m HQ relocation savings provide EBITDA uplift. Net organic EBITDA change: broadly flat to modest positive given Sales headwind offsetting Lettings progress.
  • (4) Interest step-up delta: FY26e fc net borrowing £58.8m vs current £1.7m — a step-up of ~£57m. This appears implausible as a single-year drawdown; likely reflects acquisition financing. At estimated 5-6% cost of debt, incremental interest on £57m = £2.9–3.4m. This would be a meaningful drag: £3m additional interest / 294.4m shares × 0.75 (post-tax) = −0.8p EPS headwind. 🚨 Interest step-up is mandatory flagged row — net debt drawdown implied >£50m.

Implied FY26e EPS: Base 4.9p + acquisition annualisation +0.2p + organic flat + interest step-up −0.8p = ~4.3p. Current FY1 fc consensus is 5.0p. Gap of ~0.7p suggests consensus may not have fully modelled the acquisition-related interest cost increase, or assumes operational improvement offsets. This is a potential downside risk to consensus.

Note: Sharescope fc net borrowing £58.8m may partially include acquisition debt already. The interest cost concern is real and requires verification at H1 results.

3. Order book / forward work

Lettings portfolio: "portfolio of over 32,000 tenancies." Two Q1 acquisitions in Milton Keynes and Birmingham. "Pipeline of further acquisition opportunities exists and is currently being worked on."

"completing two acquisitions of leading independent agents in Milton Keynes and Birmingham, as previously announced"

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

Cost reduction programme targeting at least £3m annualised savings currently under way. Builds on £1.5m HQ relocation savings (effective Jan 2026). Key initiatives: headcount reallocation from Sales to Lettings; productivity improvements.

Renters' Rights Act implementation from 1 May 2026 expected to create growth opportunities (higher compliance requirements favourable to Foxtons' scale and expertise).

"The Group has responded to recent market headwinds with a proactive cost-reduction programme targeting at least £3m of annualised savings"

5. Capital returns and per-share items

No dividend, buyback, or per-share data in RNS.

6. Qualitative tone

CEO: "We remain confident that the resilience of our Lettings and Financial Services businesses, which represents more than two thirds of revenues, alongside work to reposition the Sales business, can continue to deliver market-leading results."

"The Sales market remains subdued and has been further affected by recent events in the Middle East, which have tempered buyer sentiment and impacted mortgage rates and availability."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Guidance phrase: "trading in line with previous expectations and full year guidance remains unchanged." Qualitative only. No numeric FY guidance restated. One year. No upgrade or downgrade signal.

Outlook assesses forward FY26 only. "In line" + costs action + Renters' Rights tailwind + no guidance cut = in-line/marginally cautious read.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — "in line with previous expectations" with qualitative positive overlays (cost savings, RRA opportunity) but no numeric upgrade and explicit Sales headwind acknowledgement. Provisional points: 0 to +3.

Divergence check: Q1 revenue −10% YoY (miss vs casual expectation), but management guided this was a comparator issue (stamp duty). Guidance reiteration post known-bad Q1 = marginally positive signal (consensus survives the weak Q1). No strong divergence — the beat/miss on Q1 is framing-dependent.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

FOXT · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 cross-check:

  • FY23: H1 £65.1m + H2 £75.3m = £140.4m. Sharescope has no explicit FY total in the data — no independent FY figure to check against. ⚠️ FY actual unavailable for FY22/FY23 — H2 taken from Sharescope H2 field, treat with caution.
  • FY24: H1 £70.9m + H2 £76.2m = £147.1m ✅ (stated in data block)
  • FY25: H1 £86.1m + H2 £86.5m = £172.6m — Sharescope shows £172.5m. Rounding ✅
  • EPS FY24: H1 1.3p + H2 1.9p = 3.2p ✅; FY25: H1 2.7p + H2 2.2p = 4.9p ✅ (Sharescope current → FY: 4.9p)
  • FY22 EPS: H1 1.1p + H2 1.9p = 3.0p. No explicit FY total to cross-check. ⚠️

EPS growth trajectory: +7%, +59%, −4% → FY26e +2%. 🟡 Volatile — FY24 was the strong year; FY25 actually dipped −4%; FY26e essentially flat at +2%.

Acceleration flags:

  • Revenue: FY26e implied YoY +3.8% vs prior year (FY25) +5.3% → no acceleration (RNS-confirmed: Q1 revenue −10% YoY; full-year flat-to-modest, consensus-derived deceleration).
  • EPS: FY26e +2% vs prior year −4% → acceleration ✓ (recovering from negative to marginally positive — though tiny absolute improvement, direction is +ve; consensus-derived).

3.1 Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

*Implied H2: Revenue £179.1m − H1 baseline £85.1m = £94.0m (consensus-derived). EPS: 5.0p − 1.975p = 3.025p implied H2.

H2 derivation workings: FY26 H1 baseline = 3yr avg H1% × FY1fc. Implied H2 = FY1fc − H1 baseline.

EPS trajectory (last 3 HoH YoY figures): FY24 H2 +58%; FY25 H1 +29%; FY25 H2 −27%. 🟡 Volatile — sharp deterioration in H2 FY25. The −27% H2 FY25 EPS YoY is a significant red flag — H2 FY25 delivered only 2.2p vs FY24 H2 3.0p, suggesting H2 earnings are being compressed relative to the H1 strength.

Revenue trajectory (last 3 HoH YoY figures): FY24 H2 +12%; FY25 H1 +10%; FY25 H2 +1%. 🔴 Decelerating — consistent deceleration across all three recent halves from +12% to near-flat.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Data source gate: Q1 2026 revenue of £39.6m is disclosed in RNS. However, this is Q1 only (3 months ended 31 March 2026) — not a full H1 (6 months ended 30 June 2026). Phase 3.2 requires H1 actuals. The RNS provides Q1 only — both metrics: UNTRACKABLE for H1. I can note implied Q1 run-rate context.

Q1 run-rate annualisation: £39.6m × 2 = implied H1 £79.2m vs baseline £85.1m → tracking well below baseline if Q1 run rate continues. But Q1 is always the weakest quarter (stamp duty comparator distorts FY25; Easter effect; Sales seasonal weakness). Q2 is historically stronger. Not sufficient to determine H1 tracking direction.

Revenue baseline for FY26 H1: 3yr avg H1% = 47.5%. FY26e £179.1m × 47.5% = £85.1m H1 revenue baseline. Buy trigger: £85.1m × 1.015 = £86.4m Sell trigger: £85.1m × 0.985 = £83.8m

EPS baseline for FY26 H1: 3yr avg H1% = 39.5%. FY26e 5.0p × 39.5% = 1.975p H1 EPS baseline. Buy trigger: 1.975p × 1.015 = 2.005p Sell trigger: 1.975p × 0.985 = 1.945p

Signal: UNTRACKABLE (H1 period not yet complete — Q1 data only). H1 results expected May 2026.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-H1 mode)

H2 base figure: No updated FY figure in RNS — using FY26e consensus £179.1m / 5.0p. Flag as: consensus-derived.

Implied H2 = FY1 fc − H1 baseline (3yr avg):

  • Revenue: £179.1m − £85.1m = £94.0m implied H2
  • EPS: 5.0p − 1.975p = 3.025p implied H2

vs historical H2 actuals (last 3): Revenue: FY22 H2 £75.3m / FY23 H2 £76.2m / FY24 H2 £85.4m. Avg: £79.0m.

Implied H2 £94.0m vs avg £79.0m → +19% above 3yr avg. 🟢 moderate/strong — but worth noting FY25 H2 actual was £86.5m, itself above the 3yr avg. The consensus is pricing H2 FY26 at £94.0m which would be £7.5m (8.7%) above FY25 H2.

EPS: Historical H2 actuals: FY22 H2 1.9p / FY23 H2 1.9p / FY24 H2 3.0p. Avg: 2.27p. Implied H2 EPS 3.025p vs avg 2.27p → +33% above 3yr avg. 🟡 moderate — however FY25 H2 was only 2.2p (well below avg due to Sales market weakness), making the consensus H2 of 3.025p look very ambitious relative to the most recent H2.

🚨 Critical: The implied H2 EPS of 3.025p vs FY25 H2 actual 2.2p = +37.5% YoY improvement required. With Sales market described as "subdued" and "further affected by Middle East tensions" in Q1, the H2 EPS burden is highly ambitious. Cost savings (£3m+ annualised) are the key offset — but this equates to approximately ~0.8p EPS if fully delivered.

Classification: 🟡 moderate (revenue plausible; EPS H2 burden elevated given current Sales headwinds).

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: 5.2p → 5.0p, net change −0.2p (−3.8%) over full period. One meaningful upgrade in March 2026 (4.8p → 5.3p following FY25 results) fully reversed to 5.0p within 3 weeks. This Mar→Apr reversal is notable — likely post-FY25 results brokers upgraded then pulled back after Q1 trading update. Upgrades then immediate downgrades: net negative momentum.
  • 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (5.3p → 5.0p in last 4 weeks).
  • Revenue trend: Broadly stable at £179.1m — modest +0.4% net change.
  • Divergence: Price 83p (May 2025) → 42.7p (current) = −49% decline vs EPS consensus −3.8%. Massive price/consensus gap. Stock appears deeply discounted vs TP of 77p (80% upside). The market is pricing in considerably worse EPS delivery than consensus, likely reflecting Sales market uncertainty and acquisition integration costs.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP.

RNS-vs-forecast reconciliation: The RNS does not disclose a balance sheet figure. Sharescope current net borrowing H2 £1.7m (FY25 year-end). Sharescope fc net borrowing £58.8m — implying ~£57m net debt increase in FY26. This level of increase seems large and likely reflects Lettings acquisition financing (Milton Keynes, Birmingham + pipeline). No confirmation in RNS of acquisition consideration quantum. ⚠️ Sharescope fc net borrowing £58.8m treated as the current forecast until H1 results confirm.

  • Net borrowing: FY22 H2: −£0.8m (net cash) / FY23 H2: £6.6m / FY24 H2: −£1.3m (net cash) / FY25 H2: £1.7m → FY26e fc: £58.8m / FY27e: £46.4m
  • ND/EBITDA: 2.10x / 2.20x / 1.50x / 1.50x current → 1.60x FY26e → 1.20x FY27e
  • Interest cover: FY26e 7.9x / FY27e 11.1x
  • ND/FCF: FY26e 5.2x / FY27e 2.8x

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26e vs FY25 actual:

  • FY26e EPS 5.0p vs FY25 actual 4.9p: ✅ growing modestly +0.1p (+2%)
  • FY26e Revenue £179.1m vs FY25 actual £172.5m: ✅ growing +£6.6m (+3.8%)
  • ✅✅ FY26e EPS and Revenue growing vs prior year actual (marginally).

Step 2 — FY27e vs FY26e:

  • FY27e EPS 5.6p vs FY26e 5.0p: ✅ growing +0.6p (+12%)
  • FY27e Revenue £186.3m vs FY26e £179.1m: ✅ growing +£7.2m (+4%)
  • ✅✅ FY27e EPS and Revenue both growing vs FY26e.

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — ND/EBITDA 1.6x FY26e, 7.9x interest cover. No covenant risk visible. Monitor acquisition pace vs cash generation.

3.6 Structural/one-off flags

[Stamp duty comparator distortion]: Q1 2025 benefited from elevated transaction volumes ahead of the 31 March 2025 stamp duty deadline. The −35% Sales revenue YoY in Q1 2026 is predominantly a base effect, not underlying deterioration. Comparable to Q1 2024 on an LFL basis (Sales +£0.2m).

[Renters' Rights Act tailwind — 1 May 2026]: Implementation expected to drive demand for professional management services. Foxtons' compliance capabilities positioned as competitive advantage. Structural revenue tailwind for Lettings property management segment over medium term.

[Acquisition pipeline active]: Two completions in Q1; further pipeline "currently being worked on." Each acquisition adds incremental Lettings revenue but increases leverage.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

FOXT · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

#1 Driver — Full-year guidance survival despite weak Q1: The most important broker signal is that guidance has been maintained through a Q1 where revenue declined −10% YoY. Brokers who were concerned about Sales market deterioration will note that the comparator distortion (stamp duty in Q1 2025) explains the decline, and the LFL comparison to Q1 2024 shows essentially no deterioration. Lettings growth (+5%) confirms the recurring revenue engine is intact. This prevents a downgrade at this stage.

#2 Driver — Cost reduction programme (£3m+) and HQ savings (£1.5m): Total annualised savings targeted at £4.5m+. At Foxtons' operating leverage, £4.5m savings = approximately 1.5p EPS benefit if fully delivered. This is the key broker revision driver — whether they embed the cost savings or discount them. The EPS bridge concern (interest step-up on acquisitions) may offset part of this saving, creating a net-neutral to marginally positive revision picture.

Forecast revisions:

  • Revenue FY26e: hold around £179.1m (−0 to −2%). Q1 run-rate suggests H1 may miss £85.1m baseline, but Q2 (spring selling season) is typically stronger. Direction: hold.
  • Revenue FY27e: hold at £186.3m — longer-dated; no new data.
  • EPS FY26e: small downside risk. Interest cost on acquisitions may not be fully modelled at £58.8m net debt. Range: hold to −5% (5.0p → 4.7–5.0p).
  • EPS FY27e: hold at 5.6p — cost saves and Lettings growth supports recovery.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 77p vs current 42.7p (80% upside). Brokers unlikely to cut TP at Q1 update — the in-line signal doesn't justify cuts. Direction: hold TP or minor upward revision if cost saves are highlighted positively. No recommendation change expected.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Full year guidance remains unchanged" after a −10% Q1 is a positive signal. This language is the functional equivalent of "comfortable with" — brokers historically interpret maintenance through a known-bad quarter as implicit reiteration of confidence.

Key risk: Sales market further deterioration from Middle East geopolitics, sustained elevated mortgage rates, and/or lower mortgage product availability. Management explicitly notes new buyer activity "lower than initially expected" in Q1 — this is a genuine softening signal, not just comparator noise. If Q2 Sales volume does not recover materially, H1 EPS will undershoot the 1.975p baseline.

"New buyer activity during the period was lower than initially expected, impacted by elevated levels of uncertainty stemming from recent geopolitical developments and subsequent increases in mortgage rates and lower mortgage product availability."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: hold (guidance intact, minor downside risk). Tone label must be Neutral. → 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

FOXT · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

37/100 · Confidence: 32–42 · No FX adjustment · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

ComponentPts
🟢 Lettings revenue +5% YoY; recurring revenue base intact+7
🟢 FY guidance maintained through −10% Q1 — "in line" signal positive+6
🟢 Cost programme £3m+ annualised + £1.5m HQ savings = ~1.5p EPS potential+5
🟢 Renters' Rights Act (1 May 2026) structural tailwind for Lettings management+3
🟡 In-line outlook guidance — qualitative only, no numeric guide restated−2
🟡 EPS broker momentum FALLING (5.3p → 5.0p last 4 weeks)−2
🟡 Implied H2 EPS 3.025p = +37.5% vs FY25 H2 2.2p — burden elevated−3
🔴 Sales revenue −35% Q1 YoY; "lower than initially expected" buyer activity−7
🔴 Acquisition interest step-up: fc net debt £58.8m vs current £1.7m — ~−0.8p EPS headwind not fully in consensus−6
🔴 Revenue deceleration: +11.4% → +5.3% → +3.8% — structural slowdown trajectory−5
🔴 Mortgage rates elevated + geopolitical uncertainty — Sales market headwind persisting−5
🔴 Price −49% since May 2025; EPS only −3.8% — market pricing significant downside risk−3

Raw total: 37. No FX adjustment. Final score: 37/100.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Q1 2026 Group revenue came in at £39.6m (−10% YoY), principally reflecting a −35% collapse in Sales revenue to £10.7m against an exceptionally strong Q1 2025 comparator (elevated stamp duty volumes). The primary catalyst is guidance survival — management maintained full-year expectations despite the quarter, and the LFL comparison to Q1 2024 shows Sales revenue essentially flat at £10.7m vs Q1 2024's £9.5m. Lettings, the recurring revenue core, grew +5% to £26.4m including £0.9m acquisition contribution (Milton Keynes and Birmingham lettings businesses). The Lettings engine is working as designed. The problem is scale: at Q1, Sales was only £10.7m vs Lettings £26.4m and Financial Services £2.6m — the mix is shifting towards Lettings as the strategy intends, but the absolute revenue drag from Sales is significant.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, H1 FY26 actuals are UNTRACKABLE (only Q1 data available). The critical tension in the consensus is the implied H2 EPS requirement of 3.025p, which represents +37.5% YoY vs FY25 H2's actual 2.2p. With the Sales market described as facing geopolitical headwinds and mortgage rate pressure, the H2 EPS burden is ambitious. The key offset is the cost savings programme targeting £4.5m+ annualised — approximately 1.5p EPS benefit if delivered on schedule. Additionally, the Renters' Rights Act implementation from 1 May 2026 is expected to drive incremental property management demand, directly benefiting Foxtons' Lettings margin mix. The downside risk is contained by the Lettings engine (39% of group revenue but growing) but not eliminated — if Sales volume fails to recover in Q2, H1 EPS could materially miss the 1.975p baseline.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are unlikely to revise FY26e EPS materially from the current 5.0p on this RNS — guidance maintenance preserves the consensus. However, the EPS bridge analysis suggests the acquisition debt step-up (from ~£2m to ~£59m forecast net debt) creates an interest cost headwind of ~0.8p that may not be fully modelled. The real broker action is at H1 results (expected May 2026) when actual H1 revenue, profit and net debt will allow a proper EPS bridge rebuild. TP consensus at 77p (80% implied upside at 42.7p) is unlikely to move on this quarter.

🏁 Verdict: in-line Q1 with a known-bad Sales comparator; Lettings holding up; cost action real but H2 burden elevated and acquisition interest cost a latent EPS risk. Score 37 — neutral hold, watch H1 results in May for the definitive signal on whether FY EPS consensus of 5.0p is achievable.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

HIK · Q4 · Trading Statement (Pre-H1) · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (AGM trading statement)

1. Revenue figures

FY26 guidance reiterated: Group revenue to grow in the range of 2% to 4%. No Q1 actual figures.

Implied FY26 guidance range (2–4% growth from FY25 $3,349m actual):

  • Low: $3,349m × 1.02 = $3,416.1m
  • High: $3,349m × 1.04 = $3,482.9m

vs FY26e consensus $3,466.5m — consensus within the guided range (at ~midpoint). ✅ No beat/miss vs guidance.

Segment guidance reiterated:

  • Injectables: revenue grow in low single digits; margin 27–28%
  • Branded: revenue grow 6–8%; margin ~25%
  • Hikma Rx: revenue broadly flat; margin close to 20%

"We continue to expect Group revenue to grow in the range of 2% to 4%"

2. EPS / earnings figures

FY26 Group operating profit guidance: $720m to $770m.

FY25 actual revenue $3,349m × operating margin ~24.5% (from FY25 results) = ~$820m OP (approximate). FY26 $720–770m guidance implies operating profit is LOWER than FY25. This is a significant concern — PROFIT DECLINING despite revenue growing.

🚨 EPS quality check — operating profit declining: If FY26 OP = $720–770m vs FY25 ~$820m actual, that's a −6.1% to −12.2% YoY OP decline. With revenue growing 2–4%, this implies significant margin compression. EPS bridge:

  • FY25 adj EPS 226c (actual, H1+H2)
  • FY26 operating profit midpoint $745m vs FY25 ~$820m = −9% OP decline
  • D&A: similar levels ~$180–200m
  • Net interest: negative (net debt growing → higher interest cost)
  • Tax: ~21%
  • Share count: declining (buyback)

Rough EPS: OP $745m − D&A −$185m = EBIT $560m − net interest ~$80m = PBT $480m × 79% = PAT $379m / 211m shares ≈ 179c EPS. This is materially below the Sharescope FY26e consensus of 224.7c.

🚨 Major gap: consensus EPS 224.7c vs implied from OP guidance ~179c. Either: (a) The Sharescope consensus doesn't reflect the OP guidance, OR (b) My OP calculation is wrong (FY25 OP actual ≠ ~$820m), OR (c) The OP guidance and EPS consensus use different definitions (the OP guidance is likely "core operating profit" not "group operating profit" inclusive of all items)

Let me reconsider. HIK reports "core operating profit" as the primary metric. FY25 core OP was likely different from my estimate. The guidance of $720–770m is specifically "Group operating profit" in the RNS — this is the core/adjusted figure.

The Sharescope fc PBT is $585.6m for FY26e. If core OP $745m − D&A ~$175m = EBIT ~$570m, less interest ~$70m = PBT ~$500m. Tax ~$100m = PAT ~$400m / 215m shares = ~186c. Still below 224.7c consensus.

The consensus EPS of 224.7c appears materially above what the guided OP range implies. This is a significant EPS downside risk.

Possible explanation: the Sharescope EPS figure may use a different diluted share count or EPS definition (possibly Basic vs Diluted). Let me check: FY25 H1 121c + H2 105c = 226c. FY25 actual EPS. If FY25 actual EPS was 226c and consensus for FY26 is 224.7c (essentially flat), this makes sense if OP declines slightly but buyback reduces share count.

I may be overstating the OP decline. LSEG's FY25 results would clarify FY25 actual OP. Without that data confirmed here, I'll flag the concern but not over-assert.

EPS bridge (best estimate):

  • FY25 base EPS: 226c
  • OP decline −$50–100m (midpoint): ~−21–42c at post-tax per share (using ~79% tax retention, ~215m shares)
  • Buyback benefit: $250m at ~£13.43/share = ~14.2m shares repurchased. Share count decline from 216m to ~202m = +6% per share uplift on PAT = +6% × 224c ≈ +13c
  • Interest step-up: net ~−10c
  • Net: 226c − 30c (OP) + 13c (buyback) − 10c (interest) ≈ ~199–210c

This suggests consensus 224.7c is achievable only if OP decline is at the low end ($720m) and buyback timing is front-loaded. Downside risk to consensus of ~15–25c (−7 to −11%) if OP comes in at $720m.

FY26e EPS bridge summary: New base 226c. Inorganic delta: 503B compounding wind-down (strategic decision) = negative revenue impact, limited EPS impact (low margin business). Organic EBITDA delta: OP guided $720–770m = negative vs FY25. Interest step-up: net debt growing. Net result: implied EPS 200–215c vs consensus 224.7c — potential downgrade risk of −5 to −11%.

"We continue to expect Group revenue to grow in the range of 2% to 4% and for Group operating profit to be in the range of $720 million to $770 million in 2026."

3. Order book / forward work

No formal order book. Branded MENA: "largest pharmaceutical company by sales in the region." Injectables US: Tyzavan® (vancomycin bag) demand "accelerating." Hikma Rx pipeline: licensed agreements (tapentadol), Ellipta® device partnership signed.

Pipeline positive: generic Ellipta® programme (inhalation platform) — device partnership signed with unnamed partner for US, UK, Canada, EU, MENA. Represents future revenue optionality (medium term, not FY26 driver).

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

Injectables margin guidance: 27–28% (vs FY25 core OP margin of ~27.6% per FY25 results). Essentially flat — no improvement guided.

Branded margin: ~25% — stable.

Hikma Rx margin: close to 20% — this is a step-down from FY25 Rx margin (which was approximately 22–23% based on full year results). Rx margin compression is a headwind.

Geopolitical cost pressures: "inflationary pressure, particularly linked to shipping, energy and insurance costs" — explicitly flagged. "Confident we can absorb these increased costs through strong business performance."

503B compounding wind-down: "strategic decision to wind down our 503B compounding business." This removes a small revenue stream but simplifies the business. Net: marginally negative for FY26 revenue/profit, positive for strategic focus.

5. Capital returns

Final dividend: 48 cents per share (subject to AGM approval). Full-year FY25 total dividend: 84 cents (+5% vs FY24). Sharescope fc DPS FY26e: 85.1c ≈ consistent (+1.3% growth expected).

Share buyback: $250m programme underway. To 17 April 2026: 4,374,095 shares purchased (note: RNS says "4,374,095 million" which appears to be a typo — should be 4,374,095 shares) at cost of £54.8m ($71.5m). ~$71.5m deployed of $250m = 28.6% deployed.

"Since the launch of the buyback programme on 26 February 2026 to 17 April 2026, Hikma has purchased 4,374,095 million ordinary shares at a cost of £54.8 million ($71.5 million)."

6. Qualitative tone

CEO: "Our three businesses are performing well, supported by our differentiated portfolio, recent product launches and our strong and growing commercial capabilities." "On track to deliver revenue and profit growth, in line with our full year guidance." Upbeat.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Guidance: FY26 revenue +2–4%, OP $720–770m. Reiterated (from FY25 results). Qualitative overlap: "performing well," "on track." Numeric, one year. No change.

⚠️ The OP guidance of $720–770m implies year-on-year OP decline if FY25 OP was above $770m. The guidance range appears to be below the FY25 actual OP, not a step-up. This makes the classification potentially Cautious — guidance maintained but OP declining vs prior year.

However, the RNS says "on track to deliver revenue and profit growth, in line with our full year guidance." "Revenue and profit growth" — CEO explicitly says PROFIT GROWTH. This contradicts my OP decline thesis. Resolution: either FY25 OP was below $720m (at the low end of the FY26 guidance range = guidance implies growth), OR the "profit growth" refers to adjusted EPS (post-buyback).

Per Sharescope, FY25 actual EPS was 226c and FY26e consensus 224.7c = essentially flat/slight decline. CEO language of "profit growth" may refer to operational earnings or PBT at the segment level. Without access to the FY25 full results breakdown, I'll give management benefit of doubt on "profit growth" language — the guidance is intended as growth vs FY25.

Revised interpretation: if FY25 core OP was $695–710m (in line with or slightly below the FY26 $720–770m range), then FY26 guidance = 2–11% OP growth. This would make the classification Constructive not Cautious.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — guidance reiterated with explicit "on track" language; "revenue and profit growth" CEO statement; but Hikma Rx broadly flat and OP guidance uncertainty creates ambiguity. No explicit upgrade trigger. Provisional points: +1 to +3.

Divergence check: CEO says "performing well" in Q1 — positive start. No explicit divergence. Consistent with In-line classification.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The AGM trading statement reiterates FY26 guidance: revenue +2–4% (to $3,416–3,483m, consensus $3,466.5m at midpoint) and Group operating profit $720–770m. The primary operational catalyst is Tyzavan® (RTU vancomycin bag) "accelerating demand" in Injectables US and the newly signed generic Ellipta® device partnership (US, UK, Canada, EU, MENA) which positions Hikma's inhalation platform as a significant medium-term revenue driver. The Branded MENA business is performing "very well" despite the regional geopolitical backdrop (Iran war). The headline concern is that FY26e consensus EPS 224.7c represents a −0.6% decline vs FY25's 226c — one of the rare cases where a growing-revenue company has flat-to-declining EPS consensus, reflecting margin compression in Hikma Rx and 503B wind-down costs.

Para 2 — H1 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, both H1 revenue and EPS are UNTRACKABLE (AGM statement with no P&L data). The implied H2 EPS burden (using corrected 53% H1 split) is 105.6c — essentially flat vs FY25 H2's 105c (+0.6%). This is achievable but leaves no margin for error. The bearcase is that Injectables US Tyzavan® conversion pace disappoints and Hikma Rx flat guidance misses on the downside, resulting in OP coming in at $720m rather than $745–770m — potentially a −10 to −15c EPS shortfall vs consensus. The upgrade resilience comes from three sources: buyback ($250m = ~7% EPS per share uplift), Tyzavan® acceleration, and the Branded MENA business performing consistently. The geopolitical cost pressures (shipping/energy/insurance) are manageable per management.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e EPS likely held at ~220–225c — guidance reiteration prevents a cut while no new P&L data prevents an upgrade. Revenue consensus $3,466.5m is at the midpoint of guidance and should hold. TP of £18.74 (39.5% upside at £13.43) is unlikely to move materially on an AGM statement. The EPS upgrade story for HIK is really FY27 (248.1c = +10%), driven by Ellipta® pipeline maturing, Tyzavan® full conversion, and Branded continuing to compound at 6–8%. The current stock price of £13.43 vs 39.5% implied upside to TP suggests the market is applying a sceptical discount that will only lift on H1 results evidence.

🏁 Verdict: guidance reiteration with credible segment execution; Tyzavan® and Ellipta® are genuine medium-term catalysts; but EPS consensus is flat to declining in FY26 and the market's −46% price decline vs consensus reflects legitimate concerns about margin compression; score 43 — neutral hold pending H1 results for first evidence on OP delivery vs the $720–770m range.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

LSEG · Q4 · Trading Statement (Pre-H1) · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Trading Statement for Q1 2026, AGM statement)

1. Revenue figures

No Q1 revenue figures disclosed. The RNS is an AGM-style trading statement. Full year FY26 guidance reiterated: organic constant currency revenue growth of 6.5–7.5% (from FY25 results press release; this Q1 statement says guidance is on track). No specific H1 or Q1 revenue number.

FY25 reported revenue (from Sharescope current = FY25 actual): £9,346m. Applying 6.5–7.5% CC organic growth:

  • Low end: £9,346m × 1.065 = £9,953m (CC)
  • High end: £9,346m × 1.075 = £10,047m (CC)

At current GBP/USD 1.3515 vs prior avg 1.278 (GBP +5.7% stronger), ~50% USD revenues → headline revenue ~3% lower than CC:

  • Reported guidance range: ~£9,653–£9,745m
  • vs FY26e consensus £9,878.2m — consensus appears to be ABOVE the implied reported range at current spot rate. Potential downside to consensus of ~−£133m to −£225m if GBP stays at 1.35.

Note: The Q1 trading statement RNS doesn't explicitly restate the CC guidance figures — these are derived from the FY25 preliminary results RNS.

2. EPS / earnings figures

No EPS data. The statement says the group is "on track to deliver revenue and profit growth, in line with our full year guidance." Full year guidance: Group operating profit in the range of $720–770m (per FY25 results).

Wait — that's HIK's guidance. Let me re-read LSEG. LSEG's statement: "Group full year outlook unchanged" — refers to organic CC revenue growth of 6.5–7.5% and underlying EBITDA margin expansion. No specific EPS guidance restated.

FY26e EPS bridge:

  • (1) New base EPS FY25 actual: 418.2p (H1 207.7p + H2 210.5p)
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: No major new acquisitions in Q1. LSEG sold Acadia (agreed sale completed 2025). Net: small positive from any partial-year disposals anniversary. Approximately +0 to +5p.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth: CC revenue +6.5–7.5% × ~47% EBITDA margin = incremental EBITDA ~£280–330m. Post D&A/interest/tax and on ~490m diluted shares (post-buybacks): ~+15–25p EPS uplift from organic growth.
  • (4) Interest step-up: Incremental debt ~£5.8bn at ~5% = £290m gross interest incremental. However this is partly offset by buyback EPS benefit (fewer shares). Net: interest headwind roughly offset by share count reduction. Net delta: approximately 0 to −5p.
  • (5) FX headwind: GBP +5.7% vs avg on 50% USD revenues = ~2.8% reported revenue headwind = ~£276m revenue at risk. At ~47% EBITDA margin: ~£130m EBITDA at risk. Post-tax: ~£101m / 490m shares = ~21p EPS headwind from FX translation.

Implied FY26e EPS: 418.2p + 20p (organic) − 21p (FX) − 5p (interest net) + 5p (buyback share reduction) = ~417–425p. vs Sharescope FY1 fc 470.3p. Gap of ~45–53p — significant. The consensus appears to embed less FX headwind than current spot implies, or uses a more favourable FX assumption.

This suggests consensus EPS of 470.3p is optimistic at current GBP/USD levels — or that LSEG hedges a significant portion of USD revenue. The EPS bridge indicates meaningful downside risk to consensus if GBP/USD stays at 1.35 for FY26.

3. Order book / forward work

No order book data in this brief trading statement.

ASV (Annual Subscription Value) — referenced in FY25 results as the key SaaS-type metric: ASV growth 5.8% at H1 2025. No updated ASV figure in this Q1 statement.

ARR coverage note: LSEG's Data & Analytics division has ≥80% subscription revenues. Per ARR/subscription coverage rule: ASV is the appropriate metric (not performance obligation backlog). ASV +5.8% at H1 2025 provides visibility. No updated figure here.

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

CCC · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update

  1. Revenue — Q1 characterisation: Group Technology Sourcing revenue "increased particularly strongly" in Q1; Group Services revenue "ahead of last year." No precise Q1 revenue figure disclosed. The RNS characterises performance as "significantly ahead of the prior year and well above our expectations." "The Group delivered a strong performance during the first quarter, which was significantly ahead of the prior year and well above our expectations."
  2. H1 guidance — explicit upgrade signal: The company states it now expects "a much stronger performance in the first half of the year than previously anticipated." This is a direct H1 upgrade statement. No numeric H1 figure given. "Looking to 2026, we now expect to deliver a much stronger performance in the first half of the year than previously anticipated."
  3. Full-year guidance — "comfortably ahead of market expectations": The company explicitly guides full-year results "comfortably ahead of market expectations." Consensus PBT cited as £291.3m (range £284.5m–£297.1m). "Comfortably ahead" language implies at minimum £300m+ PBT, with the upper end likely exceeding £310m. The FY26fc consensus PBT in Sharescope is £293.8m — "comfortably ahead" of this implies a material upgrade. "We now anticipate delivering full-year results comfortably ahead of market expectations." FY26e PBT implied: If "comfortably ahead" = +5–8% above the £291.3m midpoint, that implies £305–315m PBT vs consensus £291.3m = +5–8% PBT beat implied. Sharescope FY26fc EPS = 191.3p — applying a proportional 5–8% uplift implies revised FY26 EPS of approximately 200–206p, versus current consensus 191.3p.
  4. FY26e EPS bridge (FY26 → FY27):
    • New base FY26 EPS actual: estimated ~200–206p (post-upgrade; pre-RNS consensus was 191.3p)
    • Inorganic annualisation delta: nil — no acquisition disclosed
    • Organic growth delta: FY27 consensus EPS 204.5p is based on stale FY26 base of 191.3p. With FY26 base now ~202p (midpoint), FY27 consensus effectively represents flat to slight decline on the revised base — brokers will need to raise FY27.
    • Interest step-up delta: Net cash position deepening; interest income likely rising, not a drag.
    • Implied FY27 EPS revised: if brokers lift FY26 by ~+10p to ~200p and apply modest organic growth, FY27 could move to 215–225p vs stale consensus 204.5p = +5–10% FY27 upgrade implied.
  5. Order book / forward visibility: Committed product order backlog "remained strong" at quarter end. Some customers ordering "further in advance than usual to secure supply given hardware component shortages." This creates a visibility tailwind for H1 but a potential H2 timing risk. "At the end of the quarter our committed product order backlog across all regions remained strong, reflecting good order intake during the quarter, with some customers ordering IT product further in advance than usual to secure supply, given hardware component shortages currently affecting the IT industry."
  6. Regional drivers: North America — "excellent first quarter," record product order backlog at end of 2025, strong hyperscale customer volumes, Technology Sourcing + Professional Services both strong. UK — "excellent growth in Technology Sourcing including AI-related project completions." Germany — "solid performance," Technology Sourcing good, Professional Services "subdued." Western Europe — "small improvement."
  7. Macro caveat / H2 risk: Management explicitly flags "tougher comparative in the second half of the year" and "mindful of uncertain macroeconomic and geopolitical environment." This is a deliberate tempering of H2 expectations. "We remain mindful of the uncertain macroeconomic and geopolitical environment and a tougher comparative in the second half of the year."
  8. Hardware component shortages: Noted as a current factor causing some customers to order "further in advance than usual." This could pull forward H1 revenue at the expense of H2.

EPS quality check: No EPS figure disclosed (trading update). No tax rate distortion applicable. No one-off credits flagged. Guidance is on PBT basis — clean signal.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

  • Forward-looking language: "comfortably ahead of market expectations" for full year + "much stronger H1 than previously anticipated."
  • Numeric guidance: yes — PBT consensus cited at £291.3m with "comfortably ahead" language.
  • Coverage: full year FY26.
  • H2 caveat: present but does not negate the upgrade signal.
  • Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering (+12 to +15 pts). Explicit "comfortably ahead" language with cited consensus figure = textbook upgrade-triggering language. Provisional: +14 pts.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

MNDI · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Q1 2026 Trading Update)

  1. Q1 2026 EBITDA — explicit figure, YoY miss: Q1 2026 underlying EBITDA = €212m (including €8m forestry fair value gain). Prior year Q1 2025 = €290m (including €2m forestry fair value gain). YoY decline = −26.9%. Ex-forestry: Q1 2026 = €204m vs Q1 2025 = €288m = −29.2% ex-forestry. "Market conditions in the first quarter of 2026 remained challenging resulting in an underlying EBITDA of €212 million, including €8 million of forestry fair value gain (Q4 2025 €214 million, including €1 million of forestry fair value gain)." vs consensus: FY26fc EBITDA consensus = €962.5m. Simple quarterly run-rate from Q1: €212m × 4 = €848m vs €962.5m consensus = Q1 annualised is ~12% below FY26 EBITDA consensus. Market expects a significant H2 recovery — Q1 alone is a negative read-through.
  2. Sequential comparison — marginal stability: Q4 2025 EBITDA = €214m; Q1 2026 = €212m. Broadly flat sequentially. This means EBITDA has been running at ~€210–215m per quarter for two consecutive quarters while consensus requires a large H2 uplift to reach €962.5m. Implied H2 requirement = €962.5m − (Q1 + Q2 est.) ≈ very elevated.
  3. Volume trends — positive but offset by pricing: Corrugated Packaging and Flexible Packaging volumes increased sequentially, supported by capacity expansions. However, "lower average selling prices" offset volume gains. No numeric volume or price figure given. "On a sequential basis, our Corrugated Packaging and Flexible Packaging business units increased sales volumes across our range of paper grades... The increase in volumes was offset by lower average selling prices."
  4. Energy/input cost escalation — Q2 and Q3 headwind: "Towards the end of the quarter, higher energy-related input costs" began to weigh. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East cited as driver. Pricing actions initiated but "customary lag" — impact expected to take "full effect in the third quarter." "We expect the impact of these price increases to take full effect in the third quarter of this year." This means Q2 will also be impacted by the cost-price lag — a direct negative for H1 EBITDA.
  5. Forestry fair value guidance — nil for full year 2026: Following a recent reduction in wood prices in South Africa, the full-year forestry fair value gain for 2026 is expected to be nil (vs €39m in FY25: Q1 €2m + Q2 €16m + Q3 €20m + Q4 €1m = €39m). This is a €39m headwind to reported EBITDA in FY26. "Following a recent reduction in wood prices in South Africa, and assuming the market environment does not change significantly for the remainder of the year, the full-year forestry fair value gain for 2026 is expected to be nil."
  6. Plant closures — restructuring actions: Three further converting plant closures announced (Consumer Flexibles Hungary + Corrugated Solutions Poland + Germany). Total headcount reduction: 450. Total recent closures: six plants. "In April, we announced the closure of a further three converting plants comprising a Consumer Flexibles plant in Hungary and Corrugated Solutions plants in Poland and Germany. Together these closures will reduce headcount by 450 over the course of this year." This implies restructuring charges in FY26. Positive medium-term margin impact but near-term cash cost.
  7. Q2 headwinds persist: CEO explicitly states: "These pressures persist into the second quarter and we are taking pricing actions to mitigate their impact." "These pressures persist into the second quarter and we are taking pricing actions to mitigate their impact."
  8. FY26e EPS bridge (FY26 → FY27):
    • New FY26 base: consensus 49.8p — this is already heavily downgraded and may still be too high given Q1 run-rate.
    • Inorganic annualisation delta: nil
    • Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY27fc EBITDA = €1,143.1m vs FY26fc €962.5m = +18.8%. This implies brokers expect a substantial FY27 recovery. Applied to a revised FY26 base, the quantum depends on whether FY26 needs further cuts.
    • Interest delta: ND/FCF 13.5x and interest cover 3.6x — interest burden is significant. Finance costs likely stable to marginally rising with debt at €2,515m.
    • Implied: if FY26 EPS is cut to ~40–45p (based on Q1 run-rate), FY27 at 77.4p would represent +70–90% recovery — which may be achievable given pricing actions and H2 cost recovery, but carries high uncertainty.

EPS quality check: No EPS figure in this update. Consistency check against EBITDA run-rate: Q1 annualised EBITDA of €848m vs FY26fc €962.5m suggests FY26 EPS consensus of 49.8p is at risk of further cuts. Q1 ex-forestry = €204m; annualised ex-forestry = €816m vs FY26fc consensus implying meaningful H2 recovery.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

  • Q2 headwinds persist explicitly.
  • Pricing actions initiated but "customary lag" — full effect Q3.
  • No numeric FY26 guidance.
  • Forestry fair value guided to nil (€39m headwind).
  • Six plant closures — restructuring charges in numbers.
  • Classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning — sequential EBITDA running at €212m (annualised €848m vs consensus €962.5m = −12% annualised), Q2 headwinds explicitly persistent, forestry gain eliminated, cost pressures ongoing.
  • Provisional: −13 pts
